data.title: Stability by Design
data.author: potetm
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了动态类型语言中库的稳定性问题，并以Clojure为例，展示了其生态系统的稳定性。作者引用了Clojure社区对稳定性的赞誉，并通过Clojure及其库的代码引入和保留图表，以及Fusebox库的维护实例，证明了Clojure库的稳定性。文章指出，尽管Clojure是动态类型语言，但其惯例和实践使其具有类似静态语言的稳定性。Clojure程序主要由命名空间、函数和数据构成，避免了猴子补丁和对象序列化问题，这使得代码更易预测和维护。这种文化和实践使得Clojure在动态类型语言中显得与众不同，并保持了高度的稳定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件库API的稳定性和演进策略

不同观点：
• Animats认为Rust 3D图形栈的API不稳定，频繁的重大更改（如重构和重命名）导致用户代码需要不断调整，且不同库之间缺乏协调，导致用户在使用过程中遇到很多问题和困扰。
• munificent指出，持续添加新函数而不更改现有函数可以避免破坏用户代码，但也会导致函数名称越来越长、功能相似但略有不同的函数增多。他个人倾向于让API反映作者当前解决问题的最佳方式，并通过版本控制让用户选择使用旧版本。
• lelanthran认为，API频繁更改并非正常现象，尤其是在成熟工程师参与设计的情况下。他指出，在2014年之前，软件升级带来的破坏性更改较少见，且C依赖图的小而浅使得旧代码仍能运行。
• 0xDEAFBEAD对Clojure社区将函数参数从命名参数改为单个哈希表的策略提出质疑，认为这可能会导致更难诊断的问题，并询问这种更改是否有充分的文档和测试覆盖。
• JackSlateur建议通过保留旧函数作为兼容层，同时引入新函数来实现功能升级，从而避免破坏现有用户代码。
• RandomWorker赞赏Clojure的稳定性，认为其避免了频繁的破坏性更改，使得项目在多年后仍能顺利运行，并对比了其之前在PHP、Perl、Java和Python等语言中的经验。
• benrutter对Clojure图表表示的稳定性持怀疑态度，认为代码的积累不一定是好事，支持通过严格的语义版本控制进行重构以避免代码变得难以维护或替换。
• kazinator指出，代码行数的变化不能直接反映稳定性，小范围的代码更改也可能破坏稳定性，而完整的重写可能完全向后兼容。
• globnomulous强调API接口的稳定性至关重要，更改行为和接口需要充分的理由和共识，以避免给用户带来困扰。
• juancn认为，图表反映的可能是开发者对更改代码的畏惧而非库的稳定性，并提出Scala可能因为更改安全而更容易保持稳定。
• boxed反驳对非Clojure程序员的刻板印象，认为所有程序员都重视向后兼容性。
• andai分享了Zig语言在游戏开发中遇到的编译器更改导致代码失效的经历，认为即使是“无聊”的语言在特定情况下也可能带来困扰。
• alexjurkiewicz认为，任何语言的主要库的代码保留图表可能相似，项目的代码积累和重写次数可能反映生态系统的稳定性或语言的bug修复需求。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个语言和库的比较，如Rust、Clojure、Scala、Zig等，反映了不同语言社区在API稳定性和演进策略上的差异和挑战。
• 争议的焦点在于API更改的必要性和方式，包括是否应通过重构提升代码质量，还是应通过严格的版本控制避免破坏用户代码。
• 另一个值得注意的点是不同开发者对“稳定性”的理解和期望可能不同，部分人重视新功能和改进，而另一些人则强调代码的长期可维护性和兼容性。

43930584.article_content:
I recently came across the following tweet from OneHappyFellow
1
:
I think I figured out whatâs stressing me out about programming in dynamically typed languages:
Itâs about always being unsure if using a library in a particular way is going to work and if minor version upgrades arenât going to break your code.
— One Happy Fellow (@onehappyfellow)
May 5, 2025
I found this tweet interesting because the language I use the mostâClojureâis both dynamic and yet the ecosystem has a
very
strong reputation for stability. Before diving into why exactly this is the case, allow me to present some evidence to justify this belief.
Are Clojure Libraries Stable?
I searched the
Clojurians Slack
for the word "stability," and out of 20 total posts on the first page, 8 are applauding the stability that Clojure brings. This slack is the main forum for Clojurians, and it includes discussions about various libraries, bugs, fixes, etc, therefore one would reasonably expect stability
complaints
to dominate the discussion. My search is obviously not a random sampling, but it should give you an idea of how much the community appreciates and celebrates stability.
As further evidence, consider the following two charts from
A History of Clojure
which detail the introduction and retention of new code by release for both Clojure and for Scala.
Clojure codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
Scala codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
While this doesn't necessarily translate to
library
stability, it's reasonable to assume that the attitude of the Clojure maintainers will seep into the community. And that assumption is true.
Let's look at the retention of code for various popular libraries. I selected the following libraries off the top of my head with three criteria: all have more than 500 stars and are in active use. I could have easily selected more.
xforms codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
Component codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
Instaparse codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
core.match codebaseâIntroduction and retention of code
Clearly library authors follow in the footsteps of the Clojure maintainers in this regard.
The last evidence I will give is anecdotal, but informative. I recently
pushed an update
to my fault tolerance library,
Fusebox
. This update came about because of a quirk in the retry utility. Whenever an exception is thrown, the exception is wrapped with metadata from the retry utility (e.g. how many retries happened) and then re-thrown.
A fusebox user, Martin Kavalar, recently requested that the exception be wrapped only if a retry actually happened. Not only was this a reasonable request, but this probably should have been the behavior from the beginning. I would even go so far as to call this a bug.
However, this is a bug that people have dealt with. They've written their code in such a way as to handle this bug. In other words, if I were to do the "right" thing and "fix" the bug, I would be breaking
somebody else's
code.
I told Martin as much, and he agreed without hesitation that we needed to find a solution that didn't break current users' code. This is
not
a normal interaction amongst software engineersâa breed infamous for their long, drawn out debates on the most minute of details. However, this is absolutely expected in the Clojure community.
Having given the evidence that, in practice, Clojure libraries tend to be very stable, the question becomes, "How is this possible?" On the surface, OneHappyFellow's reasoning makes sense: static types tell you when a breaking change has occurred, therefore they make the upgrade process much easier. The answer to this riddle has two parts.
What Makes Clojure Different?
In short, Clojure isâby conventionâthe most static dynamic language in existence.
In his twitter thread, OneHappyFellow argues a couple of smaller points: dynamic language serialization
is busted
, and monkey patching makes it a nightmare to
pass objects across processes
.
Consider a typical Javascript program. What is it comprised of? Objects, objects, and more objects. Members of those objects must be either introspected or divined. Worse, it's normal to monkeypatch those objects, so the object members may (or may not) change over time.
Now, consider a typical Clojure program. What is it comprised of? Namespaces. Those namespaces contain functions and data. Functions may be dynamically generated (via macros), but it is
extremely
rare to "monkeypatch" a namespace.
2
If you want to know what functions are available in a namespace, you can simply read the source file.
What's more, you
never
serialize a namespace. That doesn't even make sense. Rather, you serialize data, and
all
Clojure data is serializable out of the box. In fact, it's serialized in the exact same way you write it in your source code, in a format called
Extensible Data Notation (EDN)
. EDN even lets you to create custom tags that allow you to use custom constructors for da

data.title: My stackoverflow question was closed so here's a blog post about CoreWCF
data.author: eterm
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在使用CoreWCF进行远程过程调用（RPC）和进程间通信时遇到的问题。作者的StackOverflow问题因包含外部链接而被关闭，因此他决定写一篇博客详细说明问题。他试图在.NET Framework和.NET 8之间通过WCF流式传输随机数，但遇到服务在客户端关闭后仍消耗CPU的问题。作者提供了简化的代码示例，展示了WCF服务和gRPC的对比，并解释了其WCF服务的实现细节，包括自定义的随机数流类`RandomStream`。他怀疑问题可能源于对WCF流的误解，并希望通过这篇博客找到解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：StackOverflow平台的变化及适用性，特别是在处理CoreWCF和高CPU占用问题上的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[eterm]** 认为StackOverflow不再适合提问技术问题，因为其问题被关闭，因此选择在博客上发泄不满，并提供了其StackOverflow问题的链接，希望获得反馈。
• **[hakunin]** 分享了自己在StackOverflow上的经历，提到好的答案有时会被社区机器人删除，并举例说明自己如何将答案保存在个人博客中。
• **[bytefish]** 建议直接在CoreWCF的issue tracker上提交问题，认为这是更合适的渠道，并提到GitHub的讨论功能也可以用来提问更自由形式的问题。
• **[darrylb42]** 从技术角度分析了问题，引用了SOAP规范，指出流式传输在SOAP和WCF中可能不支持无限流，并分享了自己在NetTcp绑定上的实验结果。
• **[palata]** 批评了StackOverflow的审核机制，认为其变得越来越有毒，导致自己停止在平台上贡献内容，并指出这是由于审核问题而非LLMs。
• **[phkahler]** 认为StackOverflow正在转型为一个精选信息源，而不是一个适合提问的平台，并提到某些知名用户的存在影响了问答质量。
• **[yakz]** 提供了技术上的建议，指出可以通过处理某些事件来取消流。
• **[cadamsdotcom]** 提出了实现`IClosableStream`接口的可能性，以便在流结束时通知服务器或客户端。
• **[eYrKEC2]** 认为尽管StackOverflow上有很多负面的人，但仍然可以从中学到有价值的东西。
• **[dkackman11]** 简单指出SO社区没有理解当前情况。
• **[jiggawatts]** 认为提问者遇到了一个bug，但这个问题不应该在StackOverflow上提出，而应该在CoreWCF的GitHub issue tracker上提出，并详细分析了WCF在流式传输上的限制和设计缺陷。
• **[incoming1211]** 认为StackOverflow已经不如从前，用户更多地关注于游戏规则或执行自己的规则解释。
• **[BrandoElFollito]** 分享了自己在StackOverflow上的经历，提到在高声望值后对平台的不满，并比较了其他Stack Exchange网站的良好体验。
• **[neonsunset]** 建议将问题提交到CoreWCF的GitHub，尽管不确定CoreWCF维护者的活跃度。

补充讨论：
- StackOverflow的审核机制和社区文化受到了广泛批评，许多用户认为其不再适合提问技术问题。
- 对于CoreWCF流式传输的技术讨论，提供了多种技术解决方案和替代渠道，如GitHub issue tracker和个人博客。
- 争议的焦点在于StackOverflow的定位变化以及审核机制的严格和不透明，导致用户流失和不满。

richardcocks
2025-05-08 My stackoverflow question was closed, so here's a blog post about CoreWCF
I'm preparing a blog post on remote procedure calls (RPC) and Interprocess Communication between .NET Framework and dotnet 8, but while doing so I ran into an issue with a service getting stuck consuming CPU after a client has closed.
It's not a good fit for asking Claude, etc., because there's too much confusion on whether you're talking about CoreWCF, WCF client on .Net Core (
System.ServiceModel
nuget package version ), or WCF on .NET Framework (
System.ServiceModel
from the framework ). This is confusing enough for humans, let alone a machine that will happily reproduce calls and configuration from something that is almost identical, yet subtly different and incompatible.
I didn't want to raise a github issue, because I doubt I've found a bug in WCF, especially since it feels like what I'm trying to do is probably a misunderstanding of how WCF streams are supposed to work.  I'm also quickly hitting maximum message lengths, and that feels like a red flag that I'm not using it as intended.
I took my question to StackOverflow (SO). I'm not a stranger to SO, although it's been a while since I have contributed anything there. This turned out to be a mistake, because I rushed asking my question. I extracted the classes I thought were pertinent to the question and that I thought could reproduce the issue. I skipped over some boilerplate starting Kestrel, but I also included a link to my repo in case answerers wanted to see the full context of the servicescalled. I had forgotten that any external links are a big no-no in SO land, so my question immediately attracted 2 close votes.
I went back, rewrote the entire question, now with a complete minimal reproduction of the issue. Client and Server fully complete in 3 source files. It now contained all the code needed to reproduce the issue, and nothing  but that code.
Two days later my question got it's third vote for closure, and remains unanswered and now closed forever.
In my frustration I'm writing this blog post, to briefly introduce CoreWCF and hope someone will be able to answer my question about what I'm doing wrong.
Scenario
For the purpose of testing RPC throughput, I want to stream random numbers from one process to another. We can test requesting numbers call-by-call or streamed. Ideally with sequence numbers so we can also examine the reliabilty for certain transport types.
In gRPC, the proto file would look something like this:

不同观点：
• **[eterm]** 认为StackOverflow不再适合提问技术问题，因为其问题被关闭，因此选择在博客上发泄不满，并提供了其StackOverflow问题的链接，希望获得反馈。
• **[hakunin]** 分享了自己在StackOverflow上的经历，提到好的答案有时会被社区机器人删除，并举例说明自己如何将答案保存在个人博客中。
• **[bytefish]** 建议直接在CoreWCF的issue tracker上提交问题，认为这是更合适的渠道，并提到GitHub的讨论功能也可以用来提问更自由形式的问题。
• **[darrylb42]** 从技术角度分析了问题，引用了SOAP规范，指出流式传输在SOAP和WCF中可能不支持无限流，并分享了自己在NetTcp绑定上的实验结果。
• **[palata]** 批评了StackOverflow的审核机制，认为其变得越来越有毒，导致自己停止在平台上贡献内容，并指出这是由于审核问题而非LLMs。

• **[dkackman11]** 简单指出SO社区没有理解当前情况。

• **[incoming1211]** 认为StackOverflow已经不如从前，用户更多地关注于游戏规则或执行自己的规则解释。

data.title: Phoenician culture spread mainly through cultural exchange
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了腓尼基-布匿文明的文化传播方式。传统观点认为腓尼基文化的传播依赖于大规模人口迁移，但新的古DNA研究表明，这种文化实际上是通过文化交流和同化传播的。研究分析了来自地中海多个考古遗址的人类遗骸，发现布匿人的基因构成非常多样，主要包括北非和西西里-爱琴海地区的祖先，而非直接来自黎凡特的腓尼基人。这表明古代地中海社会高度互联，不同地区的人通过贸易和迁徙相互影响，形成了多元的文化背景。研究还强调了迦太基帝国的 cosmopolitan 特性，揭示了其在文化和人口历史上的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： Phoenician与Canaanite的关系及其文化传播方式

不同观点：
• Gatlin认为“Phoenician”和“Canaanite”是完全双向同义的，指的是同一群人，没有特殊的区别。他质疑为何会有两个术语描述同一群体。
• Ants_everywhere引用了研究，指出文化传播是通过动态的文化传输和同化实现的，而非大规模迁移。同时，他们质疑“文化交换”是否包含战争和奴隶制等因素，类似于亚历山大大帝传播希腊文化的方式。他们认为研究排除了大规模迁移的假设。
• 0xDEAFBEAD认为，Phoenicians在历史上的重要性可能不亚于希腊人，但由于留下的记录较少，其历史地位不如希腊人。他们推测，如果迦太基打败了罗马，Phoenicians可能会取代希腊人成为“古代地中海天才”的代表。
• Lirael对文化传播不依赖于大规模迁移的现象表示兴趣，认为这挑战了基因流动等于文化影响的假设。他们还将Phoenicians通过联系而非殖民建立身份的方式与现代网络通信相比较，并思考有多少其他古代帝国实际上是文化生态系统。

补充讨论：
• Elevaet对DNA分析技术能够揭示2500年前的亲缘关系表示惊叹，强调科技在历史研究中的重要性。
• Ohadpr以幽默方式提到Wes Anderson的电影“The Phoenician Scheme”，将讨论带入一个轻松的方向。

争议焦点：
• Ants_everywhere对“文化交换”是否包含战争和奴隶制等强制性因素提出质疑，这涉及到文化传播方式的道德和历史背景。
• Gatlin和0xDEAFBEAD对Phoenicians和希腊人的历史地位和记录数量进行比较，反映出对历史叙述和资料可得性的关注。

43899456.article_content:
Phoenician culture spread mainly through cultural exchange
Study challenges long-held assumptions about the Mediterranean Phoenician-Punic civilization, one of the most influential maritime cultures in history
April 23, 2025
Human History
Punic Necropolis of Puig des Molins on the island of Ibiza. The new ancient DNA study sequenced human remains from this and other important Phoenician-Punic Archaeological sites.
© Photo Raymar, MAEF
Punic Necropolis of Puig des Molins on the island of Ibiza. The new ancient DNA study sequenced human remains from this and other important Phoenician-Punic Archaeological sites.
© Photo Raymar, MAEF
To the point
Secret of the Phoenician-Punic civilization's success:
Their culture spread across the Mediterranean not through large-scale mass migration, but through a dynamic process of cultural transmission and assimilation.
Melting pot of ancient people:
The study found that Punic populations had a highly variable and heterogeneous genetic profile, with significant North African and Sicilian-Aegean ancestry.
Highly interconnected:
Ancient Mediterranean societies were cosmopolitan, with people from different regions trading, moving often over large distances and having offspring with each other. This provides new insights into the region's cultural and population history in the first millennium BCE.
The Phoenician culture emerged in the Bronze Age city-states of the Levant, developing prominent innovations such as the first alphabet (from which many present-day writing systems derive). By the early first millennium BCE, Phoenician cities had established a vast maritime network of trading posts as far as Iberia, spreading their culture, religion, and language throughout the central and western Mediterranean.
By the 6th century BCE, Carthage, a Phoenician coastal colony in what is now Tunisia, had risen to dominate this region. These culturally Phoenician communities associated with or ruled by Carthage became known as “Punic” by the Romans.  The Carthaginian empire left its mark in history, particularly well-known for the three large-scale “Punic Wars” with the rising Roman Republic, including the Carthaginian general Hannibal’s surprise campaign to cross the Alps.
Within the framework of the Max Planck-Harvard Research Center for the Archaeoscience of the Ancient Mediterranean, co-directed by Johannes Krause, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, and Michael McCormick of Harvard University, an international team of researchers has now presented a study on the genetic history of these ancient Mediterranean civilizations.
New perspective on the spread of Phoenician culture
Map of sites included in the aDNA study (approximately 600 BCE). The numbers indicate the number of human genomes produced from these sites.
© Harald Ringbauer
Map of sites included in the aDNA study (approximately 600 BCE). The numbers indicate the number of human genomes produced from these sites.
© Harald Ringbauer
The new study aimed to use ancient DNA to characterize Punic people's ancestry and look for genetic links between them and Levantine Phoenicians, with whom they share a common culture and language. This was made possible by sequencing and analyzing a large sample of genomes from human remains buried in 14 Phoenician and Punic Archaeological sites spanning the Levant, North Africa, Iberia, and the Mediterranean islands of Sicily, Sardinia, and Ibiza.
The researchers revealed an unexpected result. “We find surprisingly little direct genetic contribution from Levantine Phoenicians to western and central Mediterranean Punic populations,” says lead author Harald Ringbauer, who was a post-doctoral scientist at Harvard University when he began this research, and is now a group leader at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. “This provides a new perspective on how Phoenician culture spread—not through large-scale mass migration, but through a dynamic process of cultural transmission and assimilation.”
The study highlights that Punic sites were home to people with vastly different ancestry profiles. “We observe a genetic profile in the Punic world that was extraordinarily heterogeneous,” says David Reich, a professor of Genetics and Human Evolutionary Biology at Harvard University who co-led the work. “At each site, people were highly variable in their ancestry, with the largest genetic source being people similar to contemporary people of Sicily and the Aegean, and many people with significant North African associated ancestry as well.”
Ancient DNA reveals cosmopolitan nature of Punic world
Painted Ostrich egg from the Punic necropolis in Villarricos (Spain). These eggshells were a popular Punic grave good, highlighting the cultural influence spreading from North Africa.
© Museo Arqueológico Nacional Madrid
Painted Ostrich egg from the Punic necropolis in Villarricos (Spain). These eggshells were a popular Punic grave good, highlighting the cultural influence

data.title: How to start a school with your friends
data.author: geverett
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于非传统教育模式（如FractalU、Shoshin College等）的可行性、动机以及与现有教育体系的对比

不同观点：
• jbellis对描述中"极低管理 overhead"表示怀疑，引用了一个类似项目，该项目中家长志愿者承担所有行政工作，工作量巨大。jbellis根据个人经验认为后一种结果更可能发生。
• maxverse提到The Recurse Center也开始了类似的非传统教育项目，并提供了相关链接。
• flawn提到code.berlin作为一个类似的教育项目。
• yupitsme123质疑为何现在美国没有人创建新的大学，指出19世纪时很多富人创建了具有独特使命的大学，并认为现有大学模式亟待颠覆。
• ChrisMarshallNY认为建立一个以学习为中心的社区能够吸引很多人参与，但也指出并不是所有人都热爱学习，这对某些人来说可能比较沮丧。
• geverett提到纽约的一个共享居住房屋创办的‘大学’在过去两年里教授了数千名学生。
• vianarafael认为FractalU通过社区激励学习是一种对‘edtech’趋势的颠覆，并提出是否可以通过设计更好的社会学习环境来解锁学习效果。
• rahimnathwani欣赏这种‘高能动性’的帖子，认为这些项目鼓励人们主动去做事情。
• sirodoht提到受到FractalU启发，在伦敦创办了Shoshin College，并提供了相关链接。
• aspenmayer提供了一个存档链接，未做详细评论。
• pcthrowaway对"How to Live Near your Friends"一文中作者的态度表示有趣，认为作者虽然有道理，但也可以通过与邻居交朋友或搬到朋友附近来解决问题。
• sakesun幽默地指出AI可以处理其他杂务，人们可以专注于学习。
• fitsumbelay简单表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于非传统教育项目的可行性及其管理负担。jbellis引用实例质疑低管理overhead的说法，而其他参与者如geverett和sirodoht则分享了类似项目成功的案例。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是现有大学模式的颠覆性。yupitsme123提出为何现在没有人创建新的大学，并认为19世纪的大学创建潮有其独特使命，这引发了对现代大学模式的反思。
• vianarafael提出通过社区激励学习可能比单纯依靠软件（如MOOCs或LLM导师）更有效，这为教育模式的创新提供了新视角。

总结来看，评论中对非传统教育模式的支持和质疑并存，主要争议在于其可行性和管理负担，同时也讨论了现代大学模式的变革可能性和学习环境的社会设计。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iMessage使用PQ3加密协议的安全性和隐私性

不同观点：
• [contact9879] 认为该评论讨论的主题与之前的一篇论文有关，该论文在PQ3发布时首次出现，并提供了一个链接指向ePrint上的相关论文。这表明讨论的技术具有一定的学术背景，关注的是PQ3协议的技术细节和更新。

• [modeless] 提出质疑，认为尽管iMessage采用了高安全性的加密协议，但Apple默认会将用户的加密密钥备份到iCloud，这实际上削弱了安全性。他还提到这种做法一方面是为了帮助用户恢复数据，另一方面也可能是为了响应执法部门的要求提供明文数据。这里表达了对隐私泄露的担忧，尤其是涉及到执法机构获取信息的问题。

补充讨论：
• [modeless] 通过引用Apple官方支持文档来支持其观点，强调了iCloud备份可能带来的隐私风险。
• 争议的焦点在于，高安全性的加密协议与Apple的iCloud备份策略之间的矛盾。一方关注协议的技术进步，另一方则担心实际应用中的隐私泄露问题。
• 还提到了执法机构获取明文信息的可能性，这是隐私讨论中的一个敏感话题。

• 争议的焦点在于，高安全性的加密协议与Apple的iCloud备份策略之间的矛盾。一方关注协议的技术进步，另一方则担心实际应用中的隐私泄露问题。
• 还提到了执法机构获取明文信息的可能性，这是隐私讨论中的一个敏感话题。

HMS
Wager
by Alan Bellows.
HMS
Wager
by Alan Bellows.
Dead Reckoning
Long-Form/Podcast:
The 18th century misadventures of HMS Wager and her reluctant crew
Written by
Alan Bellows
•
Non-Fiction
•
September 2019
© 2019 All Rights Reserved. Do not distribute or repurpose this work without written permission from the copyright holder(s).
Printed from https://www.damninteresting.com/dead-reckoning/
Listen to Podcast
This story is assembled from contemporaneous first-person accounts. As such, quotations contain some antiquated spellings, grammar, and phrasing.
In the Earth’s extreme southern latitudes, where the Pacific and Atlantic oceans meet, there is a rocky gap of sea between Antarctica and South America known as the Drake Passage. Among 18th century seafarers, this corridor was also known by a more ghoulish nickname: The sailors’ graveyard. In the so-called Age of Exploration, the Drake Passage was the least impractical route for large European ships to travel around South America to access its west coast. The passage hooks far south⁠—almost to the Antarctic Circle⁠—to navigate around Cape Horn on the extreme southern tip of the continent. Sensible sailors avoided the corridor except in the relatively calm summer, yet on 12 April 1741⁠—deep into blustery autumn⁠—the British Royal Navy ship HMS
Wager
was at full sail in the dead center of the Drake Passage.
Aboard
Wager
, veteran ship’s gunner John Bulkeley was the officer of the watch, overseeing the ship’s navigation in the midst of a violent storm. The sky was a wet, howling tempest, the sea undulated with mountainous swells.
Wager’s
timbers creaked and her sails thrashed as the air and ocean conspired to smash the ship to pieces. Bulkeley had seen a lot of storms in his day, but nothing like this. One ocean swell⁠—the largest he had ever witnessed⁠—swept over the ship and briefly submerged
Wager
and her 160 crew in frigid water, washing Bulkeley across the quarter-deck.
Wager
had entered the Drake Passage about a month earlier. She had been accompanied by seven other Royal Navy ships, all part of a secret squadron on a wartime mission heading for Patagonia on the west coast of South America. A principal hazard in sailing westward in the Drake Passage is that the winds and currents are powerful, relentless, and moving in exactly the wrong direction. Temperatures are frosty in autumn at such a southern latitude, and precipitation is nearly constant. In the era of sailing ships, the Drake Passage was a perilous venture even for a robust vessel manned by an intrepid crew in the calm season⁠—a collection of characteristics that utterly failed to describe HMS
Wager
.
Wager’s
speed and maneuverability were compromised due to the loss of a mast in the storm. Her captain was dead, her acting captain was bedridden, and many of the men were deathly ill.
Wager
had lost contact with the other ships of the squadron, having fallen hopelessly far behind. And her crew’s troubles had only just begun.
Cape Horn from space
Wager
was a long way from where she had started life. She was originally built in 1734 for the East India Company to shuttle spices, fabrics, and other exotic goods from the Far East to England, defended by 28 cannons. Although the name “Wager” evokes images of risk-taking and swashbuckling, her namesake was mundane⁠—she was named after Admiral Sir Charles Wager, First Lord of the Admiralty of the British Royal Navy. In 1739, the same navy purchased the lightly-used cargo ship, and refitted
Wager
into His Majesty’s Ship
Wager
, a supply and support vessel. She was placed under the command of Captain Dandy Kidd, and this delightfully monikered officer’s first mission as
Wager’s
captain would be to support Commodore George Anson on a clandestine mission to surprise, harass, and plunder the enemy in the name of King George II.
The enemy in question was the Spanish Empire. Two and a half centuries earlier, Christopher Columbus had stumbled upon the Americas on behalf of Spain, and subsequently Spain established a firm foothold in the so-called “New World.” The Spanish Empire looted vast quantities of silver, spices, sugar, and tobacco, and this flow of wealth attracted the jealous attention of the British monarchy. Spain strictly limited other nations’ business in the New World, nevertheless English privateers often smuggled goods and slaves in the region. In response, the Spanish navy began patrolling these waters, asserting the right to inspect any vessels.
During one such inspection in 1731, a British merchant captain named Robert Jenkins protested the intrusion, and in the ensuing scuffle the Spanish captain’s blade somehow separated Captain Jenkins from his left ear. This civilian injury was far from newsworthy back in Britain⁠—after all, smuggling was a rough business. Eight years later, however, when Great Britain sought a pretext for war, it became politically expedient for British politicians to suffer outrage over this unauthorized amputation. Legen

data.title: eBPF Mystery: When is IPv4 not IPv4? When it's pretending to be IPv6
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary:
这篇文章描述了一次使用eBPF程序透明地重定向DNS请求的冒险经历，最初目标是重定向单个程序（或Docker容器）在端口53上的DNS请求。作者通过在cgroup上使用BPF_CGROUP_INET4_CONNECT来检查和重定向syscall.connect发生的流量。起初，一切顺利，但当用户尝试使用dotnet CLI时，程序出现了挂起问题，并产生了大量PACKET_IPV6_TYPE阻塞消息。

尽管网络流量显示为IPv4，但eBPF程序却检测到IPv6请求。通过深入研究，作者发现.NET 5之后的DualMode sockets特性允许通过IPv6套接字处理IPv4流量，这导致eBPF程序的行为异常。具体原因是IPv4-mapped IPv6地址的使用，这种地址将IPv4地址编码在IPv6地址中。

最终，通过禁用DualMode sockets特性，问题得以解决，eBPF程序正常工作。这次经历揭示了网络协议底层的一些复杂交互，特别是IPv4和IPv6的兼容性机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IPv4与IPv6地址的兼容性处理及其在不同操作系统和网络配置中的实现方式

不同观点：
• [zzq1015] 提出在Linux系统中，通过调整内核设置（`sysctl -w net.ipv6.bindv6only=1`）可以让IPv6不包含IPv4映射地址，从而实现更纯粹的IPv6使用。
• [brewmarche] 指出IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址是不同的概念，前者（::/96）已不再使用，后者（::ffff:0:0/96）则常用于同时绑定IPv4和IPv6的套接字。此外，还提到了其他将IPv4嵌入IPv6的方式，如NAT64和6to4。
• [IcePic] 认为像OpenBSD这样不允许在IPv6套接字上处理IPv4的操作系统可能有其道理。虽然让程序员只需监听一个套接字很方便，但这会导致后续处理中的复杂性，特别是在日志记录等方面。因此，强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理可能是更正确的选择。
• [degamad] 认为IPv6套接字假装成IPv4来进行路由是一种反向操作，即IPv6套接字用于处理IPv4端点的路由。
• [Almondsetat] 表示嵌入IPv4地址到IPv6字段中是Linux支持的一种正式定义的单播IPv6地址类型，并指出这是官方定义的特性，甚至在Wikipedia上也有相关描述。

补充讨论：
• [smitty1e] 分享了一个Python脚本中的类似情况，通过调用一个C程序来处理字符编码，而实际上Python的`open()`函数本身就支持编码参数，这表明有时候复杂的解决方案可能是因为不了解工具的全部功能。
• [dilfish] 提到在使用Go的`net.ListenTCP`时，通过`lsof`查看网络类型会显示为IPv6，但它也能处理IPv4请求。
• [imoverclocked] 进一步介绍了6to4和6over4的区别，指出通过嵌入全球唯一的IPv4地址可以创建自动隧道的IPv6网络。
• [gitroom] 则对所有这些让网络通信变得可能的技巧表示赞赏，并质疑这些技巧是因为习惯还是为了走捷径而存在。

争议焦点：
• IPv4映射地址在IPv6套接字中的使用是否合理，是否应该强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理，以避免潜在的复杂性和混淆。
• 对IPv4和IPv6地址嵌入技术的不同理解，特别是对IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址的区分。

BPF_CGROUP_INET4_CONNECT

cgroup
. That lets me inspect and redirect traffic when
syscall.connect
occurs from within the
cgroup
. Here is a simplified version 👇

The machines running the program don’t have IPv6 support, so my assumption was that I’d covered the bases.
I then used an
BPF_PROG_TYPE_CGROUP_SKB
eBPF program
to ensure that the redirect couldn’t be circumvented by making direct IP calls. Roughly this looked like 👇

"cgroup_skb/egress"
)

cgroup_skb_egress
(
struct
__sk_buff
*
skb
)
{
// Block IPv6 traffic. Currently not supported.
if
(
skb
->
family
==
AF_INET6
)
{
struct
event
info
=
{
...
.
eventType
=
PACKET_IPV6_TYPE
,
};
bpf_ringbuf_output
(
&
events
,
&
info
,
sizeof
(
info
),
0
);
return
EGRESS_DENY_PACKET
;
}
// .... then we'd check if outbound ip was allowed and deny/allow ...
Note: I’m using
bpf_ringbuf_output
here to track events from the eBPF program and logging them from userspace. This was invaluable for tracking down this bug, without them, it would be very hard to reason about what was happening inside the eBPF portion of the progam.
Everything was going very well,
until a user tried
dotnet
CLI.
When they ran
dotnet add package x
it would hang indefinitely and produce lots of
PACKET_IPV6_TYPE
blocked messages via the
ringbuf_output
.
Oh dotnet is using IPv6
The obvious conclusion was the machine was somehow making IPv6 requests, so I did some digging
❓ My
connect4
eBPF program was not getting hit, I added similar
bpf_ringbuf_output
events so I could stream to log in userspace
❌ Hooking up wireshark, I confirmed that
dotnet
wasn’t making IPv6 calls off the box and the box couldn’t make IPv6 requests to the internet
Now I’m baffled.
Network traffic shows IPv4 calls going out
egress
eBPF program shows IPv6
connect4
eBPF program doesn’t fire suggesting no IPv4
connect
call is made
What! These contradict each other!
Read more Kernel and
dotnet
source code
At this point I knew there must be something I was misunderstanding.
I spent a bunch of timing digging into the kernel, eBPF and
dotnet
to see if I could find anything that made the
dotnet cli
special, as no other tooling seemed to be impacted.
I started changing the program to get more info, I added a
connect6
eBPF program and hook that this would hit for
syscall.connect
on IPv6. Hopefully it would confirm thas
dotnet
was infact using IPv6 somehow?!
SEC
(
"cgroup/connect6"
)
int
connect6
(
struct
bpf_sock_addr
*
ctx
)
{
struct
event
info
=
{
.
eventType
=
IPV4_VIA_IPV6_REDIRECT_TYPE
,
};
bpf_ringbuf_output
(
&
events
,
&
info
,
sizeof
(
info
),
0
);
return
1
;
}
Running the repro steps
dotnet add package x
with the above hook, I was immediately greeted by
connect6
being hit, even though wireshark showed IPv4 traffic exiting the VM.
At this point the only conclusion I could think of was that the kernel is seeing IPv6 but the traffic is actually IPv4.
This triggered a memory about dual stack networking. Digging through
dotnet
repos I found this:
Since .NET 5, we are using DualMode sockets in SocketsHttpHandler. This allows us to handle IPv4 traffic from an IPv6 socket, and is considered to be a favorable practice by RFC 1933
link
rfc1933
The feature had a kill switch! I gave it a try, with
DualMode sockets
disabled everything worked as expected,
connect4
got hit and the
egress
didn’t see the request as being IPv6. 🚀
How the question was why? What was this feature doing under the covers.
IPv4-Compatible IPv6 Address
or “When IPv4 pretends to be IPv6 for a little bit”
This 👇 line of the
dotnet
DualMode
socket docs felt like the key 🗝
This allows us to handle IPv4 traffic from an IPv6 socket
But how! Digging more into the source and kernel I found:
IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses
This is a way to encode an IPv4 address
inside an IPv6 address
.
When used you get an IPv6 address where the last 32bits are actually a IPv4 address
.

connect6
eBPF

主要讨论点：IPv4与IPv6地址的兼容性处理及其在不同操作系统和网络配置中的实现方式

不同观点：
• [zzq1015] 提出在Linux系统中，通过调整内核设置（`sysctl -w net.ipv6.bindv6only=1`）可以让IPv6不包含IPv4映射地址，从而实现更纯粹的IPv6使用。
• [brewmarche] 指出IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址是不同的概念，前者（::/96）已不再使用，后者（::ffff:0:0/96）则常用于同时绑定IPv4和IPv6的套接字。此外，还提到了其他将IPv4嵌入IPv6的方式，如NAT64和6to4。
• [IcePic] 认为像OpenBSD这样不允许在IPv6套接字上处理IPv4的操作系统可能有其道理。虽然让程序员只需监听一个套接字很方便，但这会导致后续处理中的复杂性，特别是在日志记录等方面。因此，强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理可能是更正确的选择。
• [degamad] 认为IPv6套接字假装成IPv4来进行路由是一种反向操作，即IPv6套接字用于处理IPv4端点的路由。
• [Almondsetat] 表示嵌入IPv4地址到IPv6字段中是Linux支持的一种正式定义的单播IPv6地址类型，并指出这是官方定义的特性，甚至在Wikipedia上也有相关描述。

补充讨论：
• [smitty1e] 分享了一个Python脚本中的类似情况，通过调用一个C程序来处理字符编码，而实际上Python的`open()`函数本身就支持编码参数，这表明有时候复杂的解决方案可能是因为不了解工具的全部功能。
• [dilfish] 提到在使用Go的`net.ListenTCP`时，通过`lsof`查看网络类型会显示为IPv6，但它也能处理IPv4请求。
• [imoverclocked] 进一步介绍了6to4和6over4的区别，指出通过嵌入全球唯一的IPv4地址可以创建自动隧道的IPv6网络。
• [gitroom] 则对所有这些让网络通信变得可能的技巧表示赞赏，并质疑这些技巧是因为习惯还是为了走捷径而存在。

争议焦点：
• IPv4映射地址在IPv6套接字中的使用是否合理，是否应该强制应用程序对两种协议进行分离处理，以避免潜在的复杂性和混淆。
• 对IPv4和IPv6地址嵌入技术的不同理解，特别是对IPv4兼容地址和IPv4映射地址的区分。

data.title: Audiobookshelf: Self-hosted audiobook and podcast server
data.author: fjk
data.article_summary: Audiobookshelf 是一个自托管的音频书和播客服务器，允许用户在自己的服务器上管理和播放音频书籍及播客。文档部分提供了详细的设置和使用指南，帮助用户快速上手。常见问题解答则解决了用户在使用过程中可能遇到的各种问题。此外，用户可以通过多种方式支持该项目的发展。展示区则展示了其他用户的使用案例和成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音频书籍和播客管理的自托管解决方案，以及相关应用程序的功能和用户体验

不同观点：
• Krick认为当前的Android应用程序在控制功能上不足，特别是在回退按钮和移动特定功能（如断开耳机时停止播放、锁屏小工具、暂停后自动回退等）方面。他还强调了下载音频书籍以离线使用的需求。
• TheAceOfHearts关注元数据清理工具的改进，建议通过规则定义和增量工具来提升大 collection 的管理效率，并提出通过AI工具自动化标签处理的可能性。
• Walthamstow因Android应用程序无法排队播客而停止使用，强调在特定场景下自动播放下一集的必要性。
• Apitman正在开发一个音频书籍应用程序，并就是否集成播客功能征求意见。
• Azalemeth推荐AntennaPod作为优秀的播客管理软件，并指出其下载和元数据集成的优点。
• P0w3n3d寻找类似Spotify的自托管解决方案，但对Owncloud不感兴趣。
• Arn_Thor使用Plex及其音频书籍插件，并提到Prologue在IOS上的配合使用。
• Andnand作为自托管新手，询问如何在arm架构（Raspberry Pi）上安装软件包。
• Rft使用该软件下载和收听无视频组件的播客，并提到Music Assistant的集成。
• Midasz认为该软件是自托管世界的支柱之一，并与其他自托管服务进行比较。
• Kyriakos推荐PinePods用于播客管理，指出其跨平台支持和功能上的不足。
• InsideOutSanta寻找无DRM音频书籍的来源，以替代Audible。
• Heisenzombie质疑在自托管音频书籍服务器上复制播客的用例。
• Apitman询问关于API开发的经验。
• Gitroom希望有一个统一的解决方案来处理所有音频书籍和播客的离线同步。

补充讨论：
• 用户对播客和音频书籍管理的需求存在分歧，部分用户希望集成播客功能，而另一些用户则关注音频书籍的专用功能。
• 用户对自托管解决方案的元数据管理和离线功能有较高需求，并提出了自动化和AI工具的潜在解决方案。
• 争议的焦点在于音频书籍和播客功能是否应集成在同一应用程序中，以及现有应用程序在不同平台上的功能实现差异。
• 用户对自托管解决方案的安全性和可控性表现出较高的关注，特别是与商业服务（如Audible和Spotify）的对比。
• 对API开发的讨论可能吸引开发者社区的兴趣，并推动应用程序功能的扩展和改进。

data.title: Doge software engineer's computer infected by info-stealing malware
data.author: lysp
data.article_summary: 一名在网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）及政府效率部门（DOGE）工作的软件工程师凯尔·舒特（Kyle Schutt）的登录信息多次出现在信息窃取恶意软件的公开泄露中，表明他的设备近年来曾被黑客入侵。自2023年以来，舒特的用户名和密码至少四次被恶意软件日志公开，涉及多起数据泄露事件，包括Adobe、LinkedIn和Gravatar等。尽管单次泄露不一定表明个人使用了弱密码，但频繁出现表明其凭证曾多次公开暴露。若他在CISA和DOGE工作中使用了相同或相似凭证，攻击者可能已获取敏感信息。相关部门未对此事立即回应，而批评者指出DOGE在安全操作上存在诸多问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某人的设备被黑客攻击及其对安全的影响的讨论

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，糟糕的操作安全性（0pSec）可能是故意的，有人故意泄露秘密，以此作为背叛行为的借口。这种观点暗示某些人（如评论中提到的俄罗斯）可能从中获利，且以无能作为合理的否认借口。  
   （代表评论：[amelius]）

• 另一种观点质疑是否有足够的证据支持这种阴谋论，指出自己的电子邮件也曾出现在数据泄露中，而这并不能直接证明系统中存在键盘记录器。这种观点认为批评某些组织的重大失误是重要的，但这种文章降低了新闻 journalism 的可信度。  
   （代表评论：[whacko_quacko]）

• 有人批评这种推测性文章和点击诱饵式的标题，认为读者不应一再被这种垃圾信息所迷惑。  
   （代表评论：[dev_l1x_be]）

• 有评论指出，问题不仅在于密码泄露，而是涉及“窃取恶意软件”，这些恶意软件通过木马程序、钓鱼或软件漏洞感染设备，并泄露用户名和密码。  
   （代表评论：[palata]）

• 另一种观点关注安全措施的缺失，质疑为什么当事人不使用机构提供的电脑，并指出在安全系统中不应依赖简单密码，而应使用如Active Directory角色和证书等更高级的安全措施。  
   （代表评论：[ninalanyon]）

• 有人认为，这种严重无视安全、道德、法律和宪法的行为应受到严厉惩罚，甚至终身监禁。  
   （代表评论：[sys_64738]）

• 有人从个人角度出发，认为这种事件提醒自己检查密码和安全习惯，强调需要谨慎。  
   （代表评论：[gitroom]）

• 有人提出问题，是否存在某种权威机构可以剥夺那些操作安全性差的人的特权数据访问权限，例如撤销安全许可。  
   （代表评论：[ndsipa_pomu]）

• 一种怀疑论调认为，数据泄露并不罕见，质疑是否只要账户被泄露过的人都不应在政府机构工作。  
   （代表评论：[constantcrying]）

补充讨论：
• 有人以讽刺的口吻评论，认为这种事件是在为政府节省数据泄露清理的费用。  
   （代表评论：[mystified5016]）

• 有人预测相关方会隐瞒、遗漏和否认所有事实，持续数年。  
   （代表评论：[tjpnz]）

Login credentials belonging to an employee at both the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Department of Government Efficiency have appeared in multiple public leaks from info-stealer malware, a strong indication that devices belonging to him have been hacked in recent years.
Kyle Schutt is a 30-something-year-old software engineer who, according to
Dropsite News
, gained access in February to a “core financial management system” belonging to the Federal Emergency Management Agency. As an employee of DOGE, Schutt accessed FEMA’s proprietary software for managing both disaster and non-disaster funding grants. Under his role at CISA, he likely is privy to sensitive information regarding the security of civilian federal government networks and critical infrastructure throughout the US.
A steady stream of published credentials
According to journalist
Micah Lee
, user names and passwords for logging in to various accounts belonging to Schutt have been published at least four times since 2023 in logs from stealer malware. Stealer malware typically infects devices through trojanized apps, phishing, or software exploits. Besides pilfering login credentials, stealers can also log all keystrokes and capture or record screen output. The data is then sent to the attacker and, occasionally after that, can make its way into public credential dumps.
“I have no way of knowing exactly when Schutt's computer was hacked, or how many times,” Lee wrote. “I don't know nearly enough about the origins of these stealer log datasets. He might have gotten hacked years ago and the stealer log datasets were just published recently. But he also might have gotten hacked within the last few months.”
Lee went on to say that credentials belonging to a Gmail account known to belong to Schutt have appeared in 51 data breaches and five pastes tracked by breach notification service
Have I Been Pwned
. Among the breaches that supplied the credentials is one from 2013 that pilfered password data for
3 million
Adobe account holders, one in a 2016 breach that stole credentials for
164 million LinkedIn users
, a 2020 breach affecting 167 million users of Gravatar, and a breach last year of the conservative news site The Post Millennial.
As Lee notes, the presence of an individual’s credentials in such logs isn’t automatically an indication that the individual himself was compromised or used a weak password. In many cases, such data is exposed through database compromises that hit the service provider. The steady stream of published credentials for Schutt, however, is a clear indication that the credentials he has used over a decade or more have been publicly known at various points.
In the event, however, that Schutt used the same or similar credentials in systems or machines during his work at CISA and DOGE, attackers may already have been able to access sensitive information he’s privy to. And as Lee noted, the four dumps from stealer logs show that at least one of his devices was hacked at some point.
DOGE critics said Lee’s findings are consistent with other operational security gaffes by the office, such as a
website that could be edited by anyone
and unprecedented and extraordinarily broad access to government data like that stored in the
federal payroll system
.
“At this point it's difficult not to suspect their awful 0pSec is a choice, and that there are specific people (*ahem* *cough cough* the Russians *cough*) to whom they're leaking secrets, with incompetence being merely plausible deniability for their true, treasonous agenda,” one critic
wrote
on Mastodon.
Representatives at CISA and the Department of Homeland Security—the agency that oversees CISA—didn’t immediately respond to an email seeking confirmation of the report.

不同观点：
• **对量子计算持怀疑态度**：
   - [_heimdall] 认为量子计算目前像是烟雾弹，理论数学复杂且难以验证，怀疑许多研究存在数据操纵或设计缺陷，预测未来还会有更多类似问题曝光。
   - [dreamcompiler] 认为量子计算在实际应用中的工程挑战太大，短期内无法看到投资回报，甚至可能一生都无法见到。
   - [os2warpman] 指出，经过25年的发展，量子计算主要成就只是大量消耗了氦-3，远没有带来实际突破。

• **对研究数据操纵问题的失望和担忧**：
   - [krastanov] 对数据操纵问题感到失望，尤其是在年轻科学家受到影响的情况下，认为这是对科学诚信的打击。
   - [Panoramix] 认为虽然数据挑选和操纵值得质疑，但不一定会完全否定研究结果，可能仍有一定的科学价值，只是结论需要弱化。
   - [sschueller] 感到一些研究人员只是在“扮演”科学家，而不是真正做科学工作，暗示可能存在学术不端行为。

• **为量子计算辩护及解释挑战**：
   - [chermi] 强调微软的数据操纵问题不能否定整个量子计算领域，认为该领域仍在稳步进展。他详细解释了量子计算的难度、多种技术路径的探索以及在学术和工业界之间的文化冲突。
   - [teekert] 提到早在二月份就有学者对微软的研究持怀疑态度，但同时也承认在这样复杂和高风险的领域中，出现问题并不意外。

补充讨论：
• **对量子计算投资和知识产权的看法**：
   - [devwastaken] 认为现代科技的核心是知识产权，即便研究本身不成功，企业仍希望通过知识产权获利，甚至通过占有IP来阻碍他人进展。
   
• **讽刺与幽默**：
   - [russianGuy83829] 和 [trentnix] 以幽默的方式评论此事，认为这可能会成为一个有趣的视频内容或者调侃称世界末日因此推迟。

争议焦点：
• 量子计算是否只是“烟雾弹”，其理论基础和实际应用前景如何。
• 微软在量子计算研究中的数据操纵问题是否严重到影响整个领域的发展。
• 量子计算工程挑战是否能在可预见未来被克服，或是否值得长期投资。

总结：评论中对于量子计算的讨论呈现出明显的两极分化，一部分人对其前景持悲观和怀疑态度，另一部分人则为其辩护，强调其复杂性和潜在价值，同时也指出了研究中的问题和挑战。

data.title: Implementing a Struct of Arrays
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用C++26的反射机制实现一个结构体数组（Struct of Arrays, SoA），以替代传统的数组 of 结构体（Array of Structs, AoS）模式，从而提高内存使用效率和性能。文章借鉴了Andrew Kelley在Zig编译器中的优化思路，将原本组合在一起的结构体成员拆分为独立的数组存储。

文章首先解释了Zig语言中如何通过简单的代码修改实现这一优化，然后转向C++26，利用其反射特性来实现类似的`SoaVector<T>`。通过`std::meta::define_aggregate()`函数，文章展示了如何动态生成包含每个非静态数据成员指针的聚合结构体。接着，文章讨论了如何实现`push_back`和`grow`函数来管理动态数组，并确保每个数据成员数组同步增长。

文章的核心在于利用C++26的反射功能简化SoA模式的实现，避免手动处理每个成员的独立数组操作，同时提高代码的可维护性和性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++的复杂性、结构数组（SoA）与数组结构（AoS）的性能比较、元编程与编译时优化、不同语言的对比与实现

不同观点：
• PessimalDecimal认为文章展示了C++的臃肿和复杂，偏离了原本讨论存储格式效率的主题。
• Dwedit详细解释了SoA与AoS在不同访问模式下的性能差异，包括缓存利用和地址计算的优化。
• gr4vityWall提到使用Haxe宏在编译时进行AoS到SoA的转换，并对可读性提出质疑。
• ozgr4kurt质疑是否需要通过元编程来优化结构设计，认为从一开始就设计好列式存储会更好。
• perihelions展示了如何在Common Lisp中实现SoA的想法，提供了一个不同语言的视角。
• the__alchemist在Rust和Zig中使用SoA进行数值和科学计算，但对C++和文章中的抽象表示感到困惑。

补充讨论：
• monkeyelite提到“元对象协议”的概念，建议在类定义和实现之间增加一个选择布局和访问方法的阶段。
• mac3n提到JOVIAL语言的历史特性，指出其TABLE结构可以声明为SERIAL或PARALLEL。
• sph对C++代码中的特殊操作符^^type表示困惑，请求解释。
• TheHideout简化了SoA和ECS（实体组件系统）之间的类比，认为文章本质上是在讨论反射。
• gpderetta提供了一个基于模板的SoA实现，并讨论了反射的优点和复杂性。
• hinkley讨论了聚合与组合的问题，指出在某些语言中处理SoA时拥有者或类别的概念很重要。
• gwenzek认为学习Zig语言可能比学习现代C++的元编程更容易。
• adzm对文章中出现的反射和"unibrow"操作符感到新奇。

争议焦点：
• 现代C++的复杂性与元编程的实际价值：PessimalDecimal和ozgr4kurt对C++的复杂性提出质疑，而gpderetta则展示了反射和模板的潜在优势。
• SoA与AoS在实际应用中的性能优化：Dwedit详细分析了不同访问模式下的性能差异，而gr4vityWall和the__alchemist则在可读性和实现细节上提出了不同看法。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 不同编程语言中实现SoA的差异和历史背景（如JOVIAL语言的特性）。
• 实际应用中处理聚合与组合问题的重要性（hinkley的观点）。
• 学习曲线和语言复杂性对比（gwenzek的观点）。

data.title: Amazon's Vulcan Robots Now Stow Items Faster Than Humans
data.author: Luc
data.article_summary: 亚马逊的Vulcan机器人如今在存放物品速度上已超过人类。该公司一直在德国的一个仓库中测试这些机器人。与大多数专注于从箱子中拣选物品的仓库机器人不同，亚马逊的Vulcan机器人解决了将物品存入箱子的不同挑战。这一进展标志着仓储自动化技术的又一重要里程碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亚马逊仓库中机器人和人类工作分配的变化及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论认为仓库工作非常辛苦，工作条件恶劣，且不允许听音乐，只能靠饮酒等方式缓解压力。然而，这类工作对无技能人员来说仍然是一个不错的收入来源，时薪达到20美元。（ge96）
• 有人从历史角度对比，提到亨利·福特希望他的工人能够负担得起他的汽车，而如今贝索斯正用机器人取代工人，质疑未来谁来购买产品。（thisisnotauser）
• 有人指出亚马逊和Ocado在自动化仓库设计上的不同策略，亚马逊是将机器人嵌入人类设计的仓库，而Ocado是人类监督机器人仓库，后者问题相对简单。（philipwhiuk）
• 有评论关注成本问题，质疑机器人是否能降低客户的成本。（kylehotchkiss）
• 有人对工人安全表示担忧，指出曾有仓库频繁出现急救情况，批评对老年工人的虐待问题。（damion6）
• 有人以幽默方式表达对机器人引入的惊讶，特别是带有可伸缩刀片的机器人出现在仓库场景中。（omneity）
• 有人认为这是技术发展的关键时刻，预示着重大变革。（greekanalyst）

补充讨论：
• 有评论质疑当前的技术发展方向，认为应该采用类似集装箱标准化系统，而不是试图让机器学习复杂的手动包装技术。（mapt）
• 有人对机器人“真实的触感”表示困惑，质疑过去能检测施力大小的机器人是否就是“假触感”。（voidUpdate）
• 有人提出公司是否在设计更适合机器人处理的产品包装，以提高自动化效率。（matthewfelgate）
• 有人乐观认为机器人取代部分工作后，未来人们不用再从事类似奴隶般的工作，可能会有新的就业机会。（m3kw9）
• 有人引用了一个幽默的未来工厂设想，工厂只需要两个人：一个喂狗，一个确保没人碰设备。（LeonB）
• 有人质疑现代消费主义，提出是否应减少对不必要商品的购买，从根本上解决自动化带来的问题。（oxqbldpxo）

争议焦点：
• 机器人引入对就业市场的长期影响，以及是否能真正改善工人的工作条件和降低客户成本。
• 自动化技术是否是解决当前仓库工作高强度、低满意度的有效途径。
• 消费主义和商品过度生产的问题，是否应从需求端进行调整。

Amazon’s Vulcan Robots Now Stow Items Faster Than Humans
The company has been testing the bots in a warehouse in Germany
Evan Ackerman
07 May 2025
4 min read
Evan Ackerman is IEEE Spectrum’s robotics editor.
While most of warehouse robotics focuses on the problem of picking items out of bins, Amazon has also been working on stowing items in bins, which is a much different challenge.

data.title: "Night of the Living Dead" accidentally became public domain (2019)
data.author: edavis
data.article_summary: 《活死人之夜》是由乔治·罗梅罗执导的经典恐怖片，奠定了现代僵尸的形象：无智力的行尸走肉，渴望活人 flesh。该片因发行商忘记添加版权声明而进入公共领域，导致罗梅罗损失了数百万潜在收入。尽管如此，影片因其易得性而成为经典，影响了如《行尸走肉》和《僵尸之地》等众多作品。罗梅罗后续拍摄了五部僵尸电影，其中《活死人黎明》被认为是最出色的续作。尽管他在好莱坞未获足够认可，但罗梅罗作为僵尸电影教父的地位无可撼动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：版权问题的历史变化及其影响

不同观点：
• **gus_massa** 指出，1989年3月1日之后的版权作品，使用版权声明是可选的，而之前的作品若没有适当的版权声明，可能会丧失版权保护。他特别提到1978年到1989年之间的作品在缺少声明时，可能需要在一定时间内采取纠正措施，否则会丧失版权保护。作品在1978年之前出版的则受1909年版权法管辖，缺少声明将永久丧失版权保护。

• **Malic** 提到了1963年的电影《Charade》也发生了类似的情况，因为版权问题进入了公共领域。

• **mathgeek** 对“不幸的错误”使电影进入公共领域表示矛盾，质疑这是否真的不幸。

• **nico** 认为版权持续时间过长（作者生命加死后70年），对此表示质疑。

• **wodenokoto** 质疑发行商是否确实拥有电影的足够所有权，将其微改版本发布到公共领域。他提到一个类似案例，一个语言学习公司错误地将材料发布到公共领域，实际上他们并没有重新授权的权利。

• **teddyh** 不同意将《Night of the Living Dead》的版权问题与Linus Torvalds的Linux收费问题类比，认为进入公共领域帮助该电影成为经典，而不是不幸。他指出，如果该电影仍然受版权保护，可能只会成为历史脚注。

• 版权声明在不同时间段的法律效力是讨论的焦点之一，特别是历史版权法的变化对作品版权状态的影响。

43909179.article_content:
George Romero's
Night of the Living Dead
is one of the most popular horror films ever, but an unfortunate error accidentally made it public domain. With
Night of the Living Dead,
Romero created the zombie
as we know it today, a walking corpse with little intelligence that craves the flesh of the living. Without
Night of the Living Dead,
there would be no
The Walking Dead,
Zombieland,
or hundreds of other zombie movies and TV shows. When it comes to zombies, Romero is the godfather.
Romero would of course go on to direct five other zombie films, although most had no explicit connection to each other. Many would argue his greatest was
Night
's sequel,
Dawn of the Dead,
although
Day of the Dead
also has its diehard fans. While Romero might've preferred he not just be known as the guy who makes zombie movies, most of them are so good it's easy to see why he's so closely identified with the sub-genre.
Related:
10 Best Horror Movies Of The 1960s
Unfortunately, despite
Night of the Living Dead
's massive success, Romero never really got the respect from Hollywood he truly deserved, if only because his independent spirit made him reluctant to compromise his creative visions to fit studio mandates. Romero also never achieved the massive fortune he rightfully earned by co-writing and directing
Night of the Living Dead,
due to a ridiculous error by the film's initial distributor.
Night of the Living Dead's Distributor Forgot to Copyright the Film
Night of the Living Dead
today exists within the
public domain,
meaning copies of the film are free to watch and share. That's why the film has had dozens of home video releases by different companies, as all they had to do is acquire a copy of the film, and then they could freely release it without cutting any kind of deal with Romero or his collaborators.
Night of the Living Dead
being public domain is the fault of the film's distributor, who didn't put the required copyright notice on the theatrical prints. This error occurred after the film's title was changed from its original moniker
Night of the Flesh Eaters.
Prints with that title contained the copyright notice, but when new prints were created using the title
Night of the Living Dead,
the copyright notice was forgotten.
Night of the Living Dead Being Public Domain Cost George Romero Millions
As the late, great
George Romero
lamented publicly on more than one occasion,
Night of the Living Dead
's copyright snafu ended up costing him untold amounts of money in both the short and long term.
Night of the Living Dead
made over $30 million at the box office, a massive sum for the late 1960s that Romero saw little of. Romero also didn't make any money off of most of the aforementioned home video releases, outside of some by more reputable companies that saw fit to involve Romero in their products.
Night of the Living Dead
also saw multiple theatrical re-releases. Somewhat ironically though, it's
Night of the Living Dead
's freely available nature that helped it become the revered classic it is today, as easy access and constant TV airings ensured that more and more people saw the film.

Why George Romero Was Fired From the Resident Evil Movie

data.title: The Linux Kernel's PGP Web of Trust
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: Linux内核开发过程中使用PGP签名，主线维护者需在提交给Linus Torvalds的拉取请求中使用签名标签。由于密钥服务器概念存在问题，Konstantin Ryabitsev通过一个Git仓库维护相关密钥，目前有602个有效密钥。要加入该仓库，密钥需在5步信任路径内与Linus的密钥相连。当前有2个密钥因信任路径丢失受影响。GnuPG 2.4.x开始拒绝使用SHA-1算法的第三方签名，尽管这暂时不影响内核PGP密钥库，因为信任路径检查不依赖GnuPG的签名信任。然而，若全部SHA-1签名被弃用，将有大量密钥失去信任路径，包括多位知名内核开发者的密钥。为改善此问题，将在Embedded Recipes 2025会议期间举办密钥签名活动，参与者需在2025年5月12日前提交公钥。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源生态系统中的代码签名和安全机制，尤其是PGP和PKI的比较与应用

不同观点：
• seethishat提到BitKeeper和Linux内核源代码管理的历史，以及由此引发的git和签名提交的诞生。这表明早期的代码管理问题推动了现代工具的发展，并通过历史事件展示了当前工具的演变。

• notepad0x90强烈支持在FOSS（自由和开源软件）生态系统中使用PKI（公钥基础设施），而不是PGP（Pretty Good Privacy）。他指出PKI有更好的工具支持和用户体验，并且在商业系统如Windows中已经证明了其有效性。他认为PGP使用起来繁琐且容易出错，特别是在密钥管理和实际威胁应对方面不如PKI。他建议开源项目采用PKI来提高软件供应链的安全性和信任度。

• jmclnx讨论了GPG中SHA1的使用问题以及git中使用SHA1带来的复杂性，并提到他已经将自己的git提交签名改为使用ssh-ed25519。这反映了对旧有加密算法向更新、更安全算法过渡的关注和期待。

• NooneAtAll3则关注于语法问题，指出了评论中一个关于时间表述的语法错误，虽然这与主要讨论的技术问题关系不大，但也体现出对细节的关注。

补充讨论：
• PGP和PKI的比较是主要争议点。notepad0x90认为PKI更适合当前的软件环境，而PGP过于依赖用户的手动操作和正确性，存在安全风险。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于加密算法的过渡，特别是SHA1的逐步淘汰及其对现有系统的影响。
• 还提到了开源软件供应链的安全问题，以及通过采用更实际的方法如PKI来增强信任的建议。

争议焦点：PGP与PKI的优劣对比，特别是在用户体验、安全性和实际应用中的表现。

43935356.article_content:
The Linux kernel's development process makes use of PGP. The most relevant part
here is that subsystem maintainers are supposed to use signed tags in their
pull requests to Linus Torvalds. As the concept of keyservers is
considered
broken
,
Konstantin Ryabitsev maintains a collection of relevant keys in a
git
repository
.
As of today (at commit
a0bc65fb27f5033beddf9d1ad97d67c353849be2
)
there are 602 valid keys tracked in that repository. The requirement for a key
to be added there is that there must be at least one trust path from Linus
Torvalds' key to this key of length at most 5 within that keyring.
Occasionally it happens that a key loses its trust paths because someone in
these paths replaced their key, or keys expired. Currently this affects 2 keys.
However there is a problem on the horizon: GnuPG 2.4.x started to reject
third-party key signatures using the SHA-1 hash algorithm. In general that's
good,
SHA-1 isn't considered secure any more since more than 20
years
.
This doesn't directly affect the kernel-pgpkeys repo, because the trust path
checking doesn't rely on GnuPG trusting the signatures; there is a dedicated
tool that parses the keyring contents and currently accepts signatures using
SHA-1. Also signatures are not thrown away usually, but there are exceptions:
Recently Theodore Ts'o
asked to update his
certificate
.
When Konstantin imported the updated certificate GnuPG's "cleaning" was applied
which dropped all SHA-1 signatures. So Theodore Ts'o's key lost 168 signatures,
among them one by Linus Torvalds on his primary UID.
That made me wonder what would be the effect on the web of trust if all SHA-1
signatures were dropped. Here are the facts:
There are 7976 signatures tracked in the korg-pgpkeys repo that are
considered valid, 6045 of them use SHA-1.
Only considering the primary UID Linus Torvalds directly signed 40 public
keys, 38 of these using SHA-1. One of the two keys that is still "properly"
signed, doesn't sign any other key. So nearly all trust paths go through a
single key.
When not considering SHA-1 signatures there are 485 public keys without a
trust path from Linus Torvalds of length 5 or less. So today these 485
public keys would not qualify to be added to the pgpkeys git repository.
Among the people being dropped are Andrew Morton, Greg Kroah-Hartman, H.
Peter Anvin, Ingo Molnar, Junio C Hamano, Konstantin Ryabitsev, Peter
Zijlstra, Stephen Rothwell and Thomas Gleixner.
The size of the kernel strong set is reduced from 358 to 94.
If you attend
Embedded Recipes 2025
next
week, there is an opportunity to improve the situation: Together with
Ahmad
Fatoum
I'm organizing a keysigning session. If
you want to participate, send your public key to
er2025-keysigning@baylibre.com
before
2025-05-12 08:00 UTC.

data.title: WASM 2.0
data.author: lioeters
data.article_summary:
WebAssembly (Wasm) 是一种安全、可移植的低级代码格式，旨在高效执行和紧凑表示。其目标是实现高性能的网页应用，但不局限于网页，也可用于其他环境。Wasm 是一个开放标准，由 W3C 社区小组开发，本文档介绍了其 2.0 版的核心标准。

### 设计目标
- **快速、安全、便携**：接近原生性能，内存安全，防止数据损坏和安全漏洞。
- **硬件和语言无关**：支持多种现代架构和编程语言。
- **开放**：程序可以与其环境简单交互。
- **高效、可移植**：二进制格式紧凑，模块化，可流式和并行处理。

### 范围
WebAssembly 是一个虚拟指令集架构（virtual ISA），核心规范定义了指令集、二进制编码、验证和执行语义，但不包括与具体执行环境的交互。

### 安全考虑
WebAssembly 无法直接访问执行环境，所有交互需通过嵌入器提供的函数进行。嵌入器负责制定安全策略，可能需要应对侧信道攻击。

### 依赖
WebAssembly 依赖于 [IEEE-754-2019] 浮点数表示和 [UNICODE] 名称表示标准。

总结：WebAssembly 是一种跨平台、高效的代码格式，适用于多种环境，具有严格的安全和设计目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebAssembly (Wasm) 2.0 的新特性、应用现状、安全性、规范细节以及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• 对Wasm 2.0新特性的积极评价：
   - **lioeters** 总结了Wasm 2.0的主要新增特性，包括向量指令、批量内存指令、多值返回、引用类型、非陷阱转换和符号扩展指令。特别提到向量指令能加速诸如音视频编解码、机器学习和加密等计算密集型应用。
   - **AlexAltea** 对固定大小SIMD（128位宽）的引入表示欢迎，但希望看到类似ARM SVE的自适应SIMD指令，以让编译器根据主机能力最大化SIMD宽度。

• 关于Wasm学习与规范的讨论：
   - **pdubroy** 推荐了《WebAssembly from the Ground Up》这本书，通过构建简单的编译器来学习Wasm，并提供了免费样章。
   - **inoffensivename** 表示Wasm规范写得很好，虽然入门有点难，但规范非常详细，且有参考解释器和测试，对实现者很有帮助。

• 对Wasm安全性和应用现状的质疑：
   - **mountainriver** 质疑Wasm应用的实际落地情况，感觉像DAPPs一样，概念有趣但缺乏实际应用。
   - **canadiantim** 提问Wasm是否比纯JavaScript更安全。
   - **Dabbling_Dion** 认为如果没有浏览器直接支持Wasm对DOM的访问，Wasm的发展将受限，所有改进都是徒劳的。

• 对Wasm未来发展的期望与担忧：
   - **nenaoki** 提到Wasm Constant Time提案四天前被移入不活跃状态，指出该提案对防止计时攻击的重要性，并呼吁有人继续推进这一工作。
   - **Klasiaster** 认为Wasm和WASI要成为POSIX的替代方案，缺少的是动态实例化功能，即一个Wasm程序能在运行时启动另一个Wasm程序。

• 技术细节的讨论：
   - **rossant** 询问C函数返回结构体值能否编译成Wasm。
   - **anentropic** 问是否有运行时已经实现了Wasm 2.0的新特性。
   - **iFire** 提到在编写高级Wasm绑定时，只能使用int或float类型，询问是否仍然如此。

补充讨论：
• 对Wasm规范及草案的轻松评论：
   - **treetalker** 指出Wasm不是缩写而是缩合词，不应全部大写。
   - **aleksi** 对编辑草案的URL中含有"bikeshed"感到好奇。

争议焦点：

Introduction
1.1.
Introduction
WebAssembly (abbreviated Wasm
[
1
]
) is a
safe, portable, low-level code format
designed for efficient execution and compact representation.
Its main goal is to enable high performance applications on the Web, but it does not make any Web-specific assumptions or provide Web-specific features, so it can be employed in other environments as well.
WebAssembly is an open standard developed by a
W3C Community Group
.
This document describes version 2.0 (Draft 2024-12-18) of the
core
WebAssembly standard.
It is intended that it will be superseded by new incremental releases with additional features in the future.
1.1.1.
Design Goals
The design goals of WebAssembly are the following:
Fast, safe, and portable
semantics
:
Fast
: executes with near native code performance, taking advantage of capabilities common to all contemporary hardware.
Safe
: code is validated and executes in a memory-safe
[
2
]
, sandboxed environment preventing data corruption or security breaches.
Well-defined
: fully and precisely defines valid programs and their behavior in a way that is easy to reason about informally and formally.
Hardware-independent
: can be compiled on all modern architectures, desktop or mobile devices and embedded systems alike.
Language-independent
: does not privilege any particular language, programming model, or object model.
Platform-independent
: can be embedded in browsers, run as a stand-alone VM, or integrated in other environments.
Open
: programs can interoperate with their environment in a simple and universal manner.
Efficient and portable
representation
:
Compact
: has a binary format that is fast to transmit by being smaller than typical text or native code formats.
Modular
: programs can be split up in smaller parts that can be transmitted, cached, and consumed separately.
Efficient
: can be decoded, validated, and compiled in a fast single pass, equally with either just-in-time (JIT) or ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation.
Streamable
: allows decoding, validation, and compilation to begin as soon as possible, before all data has been seen.
Parallelizable
: allows decoding, validation, and compilation to be split into many independent parallel tasks.
Portable
: makes no architectural assumptions that are not broadly supported across modern hardware.
WebAssembly code is also intended to be easy to inspect and debug, especially in environments like web browsers, but such features are beyond the scope of this specification.
[
1
]
A contraction of “WebAssembly”, not an acronym, hence not using all-caps.
[
2
]
No program can break WebAssembly’s memory model. Of course, it cannot guarantee that an unsafe language compiling to WebAssembly does not corrupt its own memory layout, e.g. inside WebAssembly’s linear memory.
1.1.2.
Scope
At its core, WebAssembly is a
virtual instruction set architecture (virtual ISA)
.
As such, it has many use cases and can be embedded in many different environments.
To encompass their variety and enable maximum reuse, the WebAssembly specification is split and layered into several documents.
This document is concerned with the core ISA layer of WebAssembly.
It defines the instruction set, binary encoding, validation, and execution semantics, as well as a textual representation.
It does not, however, define how WebAssembly programs can interact with a specific environment they execute in, nor how they are invoked from such an environment.
Instead, this specification is complemented by additional documents defining interfaces to specific embedding environments such as the Web.
These will each define a WebAssembly
application programming interface (API)
suitable for a given environment.
1.1.3.
Security Considerations
WebAssembly provides no ambient access to the computing environment in which code is executed.
Any interaction with the environment, such as I/O, access to resources, or operating system calls, can only be performed by invoking
functions
provided by the
embedder
and imported into a WebAssembly
module
.
An embedder can establish security policies suitable for a respective environment by controlling or limiting which functional capabilities it makes available for import.
Such considerations are an embedder’s responsibility and the subject of
API definitions
for a specific environment.
Because WebAssembly is designed to be translated into machine code running directly on the host’s hardware, it is potentially vulnerable to side channel attacks on the hardware level.
In environments where this is a concern, an embedder may have to put suitable mitigations into place to isolate WebAssembly computations.
1.1.4.
Dependencies
WebAssembly depends on two existing standards:
[IEEE-754-2019]
, for the representation of
floating-point data
and the semantics of respective
numeric operations
.
[UNICODE]
, for the representation of import/export
names
and the
text format
.

43934711.article_summary:
WebAssembly (Wasm) 是一种安全、可移植的低级代码格式，旨在高效执行和紧凑表示。其目标是实现高性能的网页应用，但不局限于网页，也可用于其他环境。Wasm 是一个开放标准，由 W3C 社区小组开发，本文档介绍了其 2.0 版的核心标准。

### 设计目标
- **快速、安全、便携**：接近原生性能，内存安全，防止数据损坏和安全漏洞。
- **硬件和语言无关**：支持多种现代架构和编程语言。
- **开放**：程序可以与其环境简单交互。
- **高效、可移植**：二进制格式紧凑，模块化，可流式和并行处理。

### 范围
WebAssembly 是一个虚拟指令集架构（virtual ISA），核心规范定义了指令集、二进制编码、验证和执行语义，但不包括与具体执行环境的交互。

### 安全考虑
WebAssembly 无法直接访问执行环境，所有交互需通过嵌入器提供的函数进行。嵌入器负责制定安全策略，可能需要应对侧信道攻击。

### 依赖
WebAssembly 依赖于 [IEEE-754-2019] 浮点数表示和 [UNICODE] 名称表示标准。

总结：WebAssembly 是一种跨平台、高效的代码格式，适用于多种环境，具有严格的安全和设计目标。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一个Sofie系统的用户指南，介绍了其功能、安装及操作方法。此外，还提供了针对开发者的文档，说明如何为Sofie代码库做贡献。文章还列出了Sofie系统的当前、过去及未来版本信息。最后，邀请用户加入Slack社区，与其他开发者和用户交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源直播和自动化制作软件Sofie的实用性、优缺点以及应用场景

不同观点：
• [detuks] 认为设置过程不简单，文档不充分，尝试雇佣开发者协助但未果。虽然最终可能成功，但过程较为繁琐。
• [chriscjcj] 作为电视导播，关注Sofie与商业产品（如Ross OverDrive、Sony ELC、Grass Valley Ignite）的功能对比，指出自动化系统的惯性较大，但"免费"可能是驱动改变的因素。同时提到支持硬件的选择受限是开源软件的挑战。
• [stephen_g] 认为Sofie的发布很有意义，避免了购买昂贵的商业系统，并指出其后台使用CasparCG，还提到了相关的SuperConductor系统。
• [eddyg] 关注到Sofie可以控制提词器，甚至使用Joycon控制器，强调了其功能的多样性。

补充讨论：
• [k1rcher] 对如何进入该行业表示兴趣，提到通过游戏Not For Broadcast对行业产生兴趣，可能反映出新手对行业实践的浪漫化理解。
• [jlundberg] 提供了一个在瑞典Hudiksvall的现场演示机会，显示了社区中的实际开发者参与。
• [kfarr] 认为Sofie在20年前预算有限的情况下会非常有用，反映出对历史成本问题的感慨。
• [jesprenj] 询问是否有适合电台使用的开源软件，扩展了讨论到其他媒体领域。
• [infogulch] 探讨了Sofie是否适合Twitch直播，指出了现有大主播使用OBS及其自建自动化的现状。
• [hiatus] 关注动态重播功能，提出了操作员如何在直播中覆盖或更新片段的实际问题。
• [arboles] 询问是否可以编写实时着色器，涉及到技术实现的细节。

• [tdhz77] 开玩笑地说要创建一个人工智能电视台，反映了技术进步带来的新可能性。

争议焦点：
• Sofie设置的复杂性和文档的不足是用户体验上的争议点。
• 支持硬件选择受限是开源软件在实际应用中的一个痛点。
• 对于Sofie是否能适应动态直播操作（如实时重播）存在疑问，反映了其在实际应用中的局限性。

data.title: 21 GB/s CSV Parsing Using SIMD on AMD 9950X
data.author: zigzag312
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Sep软件版本0.10.0的性能优化，特别是在AMD 9950X（Zen 5）处理器上使用AVX-512指令集实现了21 GB/s的CSV解析速度。与之前的18 GB/s相比，新版本通过绕过.NET 9.0中对AVX-512掩码寄存器处理的次优代码生成，实现了显著的性能提升。文章详细比较了从Sep 0.1.0到0.10.0的性能进展，展示了从早期的7 GB/s到最新21 GB/s的提升过程。同时，作者分析了AVX-512和AVX2在9950X上的表现，发现AVX2表现更优，进而开发了一个新的AVX-512-to-256解析器，进一步提升了性能。文章通过代码和汇编分析，展示了如何通过软件优化与硬件升级共同实现性能飞跃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Intel移除AVX-512的讨论及其它相关技术优化

不同观点：
• [chao-] 认为Intel移除AVX-512是不合理的，因为当越来越多的库开始支持这一技术时，Intel却放弃了消费级CPU上的这一特性，而AMD则在消费级CPU上保留了AVX-512支持。
• [stabbles] 关注技术实现细节，提出通过单次混洗和单次比较等技巧可以优化性能，并分享了相关博客文章。
• [Aardwolf] 对Intel放弃AVX-512表示不满，并批评Intel在消费级CPU中引入效率较低的核心而非多泵技术（multi-pumping）。

补充讨论：
• [winterbloom] 提到在不到两年时间内实现了约3倍性能提升，质疑这种性能提升是否仅因硬件升级导致。
• [vessenes] 期待看到更高效的技术出现，并提到Arthur Whitney可能会对此做出回应。
• [voidUpdate] 对需要处理大量CSV文件的场景表示质疑，认为这种需求不常见。
• [criddell] 对文章中使用C#而非汇编语言实现高性能表示赞赏。
• [haberman] 对文章中未明确说明21 GB/s代码的具体操作和CSV格式细节提出质疑，认为需要更多信息来理解性能数据。
• [gitroom] 对Intel不断取消创新技术表示不满，希望Intel能坚持一项技术。
• [chpatrick] 认为现代编译器的自动向量化在某些情况下比自定义SIMD代码更有效，但对JSON解析等特定任务可能例外。
• [theropost] 表示自己有处理大量CSV文件的需求，认为提高处理速度非常重要。
• [anthk] 提到可以使用mawk等工具再次进行测试，暗示可能有更高效的解决方案。
• [constantcrying] 建议使用HDF5等更结构化的数据存储格式，认为CSV并非最佳选择，尤其在处理浮点数和元数据时。
• [imtringued] 对CSV解析性能数据的真实性提出质疑，认为未考虑实际数据解析的复杂性，且未处理引号和转义字符使得性能数据具有误导性。

争议焦点：
• Intel移除AVX-512的合理性及其对消费级CPU的影响。
• CSV解析性能数据的真实性和实际应用中的有效性。

这些观点展示了技术社区对Intel技术决策的讨论，以及对特定技术实现和优化方法的关注。

data.title: Itter.sh – Micro-Blogging via Terminal
data.author: rrr_oh_man
data.article_summary:
**itter.sh** 是一个通过 **SSH** 访问的微型博客平台，旨在提供无干扰的社交体验。用户通过终端操作，每次发布最多180字符的内容（称为"eets"），支持标签和提及。平台无浏览器和算法推送，强调简洁和高效。

**主要功能：**
1. **注册与登录**：通过 SSH 命令注册和登录。
2. **发布与互动**：使用命令发布 eets、查看时间线、关注用户等。
3. **账户管理**：编辑个人资料、查看帮助、清除屏幕等。

**技术栈**：基于 Python、AsyncSSH 和 Supabase 构建，主打怀旧终端体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个通过SSH访问的电影播放器引发的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  ◦ [VVilhelmsen] 非常喜欢这个概念，并希望它能持续活跃。
  ◦ [toshinoriyagi] 认为这种体验类似于旧时代的互联网，对比现代社交媒体，感觉更加清新。
  ◦ [flaviuspopan] 赞赏项目的名称、Logo以及Bug部分，整体体验积极。
  ◦ [joshcsimmons] 认为这种导航方式避开了现代网页的广告噪音，是体验互联网的更理智方式。

• [建设性反馈]
  ◦ [csomar] 指出SSH按键延迟和需要输入命令来导航的缺点，但总体喜欢这个概念。
  ◦ [Claudiusseibt] 希望能够注册多个SSH密钥，以防止物理丢失硬件密钥后无法访问。
  ◦ [ilvez] 提到缺少readline支持，最初以为可以直接从命令行使用。

• [技术比较]
  ◦ [solomonb] 认为这个项目基本上只是`wall`功能的重现。
  ◦ [zipping1549] 提到另一个类似项目 `https://github.com/bbj-dev/bbj`。

• [负面反馈]
  ◦ [alexrsagen] 报告无法使用，收到“用户未找到”的错误。

• [其他相关资源]
  ◦ [ramaro] 提供另一个SSH访问的资源链接：https://pico.sh/
  ◦ [solarized] 担心像这样的孤立地方无法被Wayback Machine索引内容。

补充讨论：
• [项目启发]
  ◦ [tehlike] 提到受此项目启发，正在自己的项目（pricetracker.wtf）中考虑通过Telnet或SSH访问和导航的简化终端应用。

争议焦点：
• SSH按键延迟和需要输入命令进行导航的用户体验问题，部分用户觉得影响使用感受，但也有用户表示可以接受并欣赏这个概念。

is your escape from the noise. It's a micro-blogging platform accessed entirely via

. No web browser. No JavaScript. No endless scroll of algorithmic 'content'. Just you, your trusty terminal, and 180 characters at a time ("eets"). Why? Because terminals

You'll need an SSH key. Don't have one? Generate like this:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Copy

.pub
file for registration.)

Ready to join? Use the
register:
prefix with your desired username:
ssh register:your_cool_username@app.itter.sh
Copy

Once registered, just SSH in. Type
help
for commands.
ssh your_cool_username@app.itter.sh
Copy

man itter
itter
eet <text>
-
Post an eet (max 180 chars). Supports #hashtags and @mentions.
itter
timeline [mine|all|#chan|@user] [<page>]
-
Show eets. Default: 'all', page 1.

Live timeline view. Updates automatically.

Follow a user.

Unfollow a user.
itter

View user profile (yours or another's).

-
Edit your display name or email.
itter
help
-
Show this help message in-app.
itter
clear
-
Clear the terminal screen.
itter
exit
-
Exit watch mode or disconnect from itter.sh.
$
ls /opt/itter

Python & AsyncSSH

Terminal Nostalgia

data.title: Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)是一种通过中空核心传输光信号的光纤，与传统实心玻璃或塑料核心的光纤不同。HCF的中心是空心，通常充满空气或真空，外部由特殊结构的包层包围，利用光子带隙或反共振效应引导光传输。与传统光纤相比，HCF具有更低的信号衰减，因为光在空气或真空中传输时，吸收和散射损耗更小。此外，HCF还具有更低的延迟，因为光在空气中的传播速度快于实心材料，适用于高频交易和实时通信等需要高速的应用。同时，HCF能够承受更高的功率，减少非线性效应和材料损伤风险。HCF在数据传输效率和性能方面具有显著优势，有望革新光纤通信领域。

What is Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)？
Holight Team
May 28, 2024
5:55 pm
No Comments
(Last Updated On: )
In the rapidly evolving field of
fiber optics
, one innovation stands out for its potential to revolutionize how we transmit data: hollow core fiber. Traditional optical fibers, which have been the backbone of telecommunications for decades, guide light through a solid glass or plastic core. However, hollow core fibers offer a groundbreaking alternative by channeling light through a hollow core, typically filled with air or vacuum. This unique design minimizes signal loss and dispersion, promising faster and more efficient data transmission.
But what exactly is hollow core fiber, and why is it generating so much excitement? In this post, we’ll delve into the basics of hollow core fiber technology, exploring how it works, its advantages over traditional fibers, and its potential applications. Whether you’re a tech enthusiast, a telecommunications professional, or just curious about the latest advancements in fiber optics, this comprehensive guide will provide you with everything you need to know about hollow core fiber.
What is Hollow Core Fiber？
Hollow core fiber is a type of optical fiber that guides light through a hollow central core, as opposed to the solid glass or plastic core used in traditional optical fibers. This innovative design leverages a central air or vacuum-filled core surrounded by a structured cladding that uses photonic bandgap or anti-resonant guiding mechanisms to confine and transmit light.
Key Components:
Core:
The central hollow region where light is transmitted. This core can be filled with air, vacuum, or sometimes other gases, depending on the application and design requirements.
Cladding:
Surrounds the hollow core and is engineered to guide light through the core using photonic bandgap effects or anti-resonant reflecting mechanisms. The cladding is typically made of high-purity silica with a periodic structure that creates the necessary optical properties.
Protective Layers:
Just like traditional optical fibers, hollow core fibers have protective coatings and buffer layers that protect the delicate internal structures from environmental damage, mechanical stress, and handling. These layers ensure the fiber’s durability and longevity in practical applications.
How It Differs from Traditional Solid Core Fiber
Light Propagation:
Solid Core Fiber: In traditional optical fibers, light is guided through a solid core made of glass or plastic by total internal reflection. The light travels through the material of the core, which can lead to attenuation (signal loss) due to absorption and scattering.
Hollow Core Fiber: In hollow core fibers, light is guided through a hollow core primarily by photonic bandgap effects or anti-resonant reflecting mechanisms. The light travels mostly through air or vacuum, which significantly reduces attenuation because air has lower absorption and scattering losses compared to solid materials.
Materials:
Solid Core Fiber: Typically made from high-purity silica glass or plastic.
Hollow Core Fiber: Constructed using a combination of silica glass and air or vacuum in the core.
Performance:
Solid Core Fiber: Suitable for a wide range of applications but can suffer from higher latency, higher non-linear effects, and higher dispersion.
Hollow Core Fiber: Offers lower latency, reduced non-linear effects, and lower dispersion, making it advantageous for specific high-performance applications.
Advantages of Hollow Core Fiber
Reduced Signal Loss
Hollow core fibers exhibit significantly lower attenuation compared to traditional solid core fibers because the majority of light transmission occurs through air or vacuum within the hollow core, rather than through a solid material. Air and vacuum have much lower absorption and scattering losses compared to silica or plastic, which are typically used in solid core fibers. This reduction in interaction with the core material minimizes signal degradation, allowing data to travel longer distances with less signal loss.
Lower Latency
Latency refers to the time it takes for data to travel from one point to another. Light travels faster in air (or vacuum) than it does in solid glass or plastic due to the lower refractive index of air. In hollow core fibers, the primary medium for light propagation is air, which significantly reduces the travel time for light pulses. Consequently, data transmission through hollow core fibers experiences lower latency, making these fibers particularly advantageous for applications where speed is critical, such as high-frequency trading and real-time communications.
Higher Power Handling
Hollow core fibers can handle higher power levels more effectively than solid core fibers. In solid core fibers, high-power light can cause nonlinear effects and potential damage to the core material. • exabrial：关注HCF的实际工程挑战，如如何在不压坏核心的情况下进行接续，如何在保持真空的情况下进行端接和接续等。
• eternityforest：提出HCF是否能应用于更多光纤供电（power-over-fiber）产品的问题。
• dvno42：讨论HCF在数据传输中的具体应用，如在波分复用（WDM）网络中是否能因色散问题减少而实现更紧密的通道，或在远程保护控制系统中实现更快的数据包传输。
• sunrunner：对文章链接的URL感到不安，但未具体说明原因。
• epx：关注HCF接续的难度。
• londons_explore：质疑如何对多公里长的微米宽管进行有效真空排气，认为简单的端口抽气可能不够。
• Ciunkos：认为文章内容充斥着AI生成的低质量信息，持批评态度。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点之一是HCF在实际应用中的工程挑战，如接续和端接问题。
• 另一个焦点是HCF在数据传输和网络延迟方面的潜在应用及其当前的技术限制。
• 对文章内容的质量和可信度存在一定争议，特别是Ciunkos的批评。
• 具体技术问题如真空保持和接续难度也被多次提及，显示出这些是HCF应用中的关键难题。

data.title: CryptPad: An Alternative to the Google Suite
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: CryptPad是一款注重隐私的协作办公套件，提供端到端加密，开源且支持实时编辑与协作。用户无需账户即可共享文件夹和文件，数据无法追溯到创建者，且不含追踪功能。相比Google Docs，CryptPad在保证隐私的同时不牺牲功能和易用性，支持多操作系统，具备简洁的界面和丰富的应用，如富文本编辑器、Kanban工具等。用户赞赏其安全性、开放源代码、零知识加密以及无需电子邮件地址注册的便利性，适用于学校、工作场所等多场景的文档协作。CryptPad免费且匿名，被视为Google Drive的隐私友好替代品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CryptPad作为Google生态的替代品及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持CryptPad，认为其是Google的良好替代品**：  
  - [laxmin] 强调CryptPad帮助大学摆脱Google生态，特别是在Google逐渐削减免费服务的情况下，CryptPad成为节省预算的重要工具。同时，CryptPad的“加密”特性让用户感觉更安全。
  - [rodolphoarruda] 认为CryptPad接近于他所研究的“个人数字基础设施”概念，能够提供持久性和弹性，尤其是在应对大科技公司账户取消等灾难时，CryptPad的免费服务已经足够强大。

• **对CryptPad的局限性提出质疑**：  
  - [righthand] 指出CryptPad锁定用户，提取文档时需要使用其UI进行解密，希望找到与Syncthing兼容的方案。
  - [hmsimha] 认为CryptPad在文档共享时存在安全隐患，文档链接可能会被大科技公司获取，且CryptPad团队未采取足够措施来解决此问题。
  - [Fire-Dragon-DoL] 提到CryptPad邀请新用户的过程过于复杂，普通用户难以操作。

• **对CryptPad的性能和用户体验的批评**：  
  - [ocdtrekkie] 抱怨CryptPad的加载时间过长，尤其是在公开分享的文档上。
  - [gitroom] 质疑开放工具如CryptPad是否能在非技术圈中普及，还是只能停留在小众市场。

• **其他工具的比较和推荐**：  
  - [eointierney] 推荐GNU的CRDT工具，认为其比CryptPad更强大。
  - [weinzierl] 提到其他CryptPad实例，如cryptpad.digitalcourage.de。
  - [emilfihlman] 询问CryptPad与法国/德国的docs工具的比较。
  - [mupuff1234] 质疑CryptPad为何被视为Google的替代品而非Microsoft，并指出其使用的图标问题。
  - [AdolpheGMartin] 推荐Etherpad作为替代方案。

补充讨论：
- CryptPad的优点包括其免费的1GB存储空间和强大的加密功能，但其复杂性、性能问题和安全隐患也受到关注。
- 有用户提出对开放工具普及性的担忧，以及对其他类似工具的推荐和比较。
- 安全性和用户体验是争议的焦点，特别是如何平衡加密保护与用户便利性。

总的来说，CryptPad作为Google生态的替代品受到一定支持，但其复杂性、性能和安全性问题也引起了一些批评和质疑。

data.title: Dasung Paperlike 13K is a 13.3 inch E Ink color monitor
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Dasung Paperlike 13K是一款13.3英寸的E Ink彩色显示器，分辨率为3200x2400像素，灰度内容显示可达300ppi，刷新率最高37Hz。该显示器支持USB Type-C和HDMI输入，具备触屏和反向触控功能，可连接安卓手机进行屏幕镜像。它有一个3.5毫米耳机插孔、内置扬声器和DC电源输入，配有六个物理按钮用于调节功能。机身由铝合金制成，重721克，支持VESA安装。彩色版售价749美元，黑白版售价679美元，目前已开始预售。彩色版配有前光，而黑白版没有。该显示器不完全支持苹果设备，主要兼容Windows、Linux和Android系统。预计2025年5月发货。

The
Dasung Paperlike 13K
is a monitor with a 13.3 inch, 3200 x 2400 pixel E Ink color display that can show grayscale content at 300 pixels per inch with screen refresh rates as high as 37 Hz, although those numbers will drop if you want to view color content or emphasize image quality.
Dasung first announced
earlier this month
, and now the company has
begun taking pre-orders for $749
. There’s also a preview page for an
upcoming Indieogogo campaign
. There’s also a
black-and-white only model that sells for $679
.
The monitor supports USB Type-C and HDMI input and it has a touchscreen and “reverse touch control functionality.” Basically that means that if you plug in an Android phone or another supported device, you should be able to mirror your screen to the monitor and interact with the apps on your phone by touching the monitor.
There’s also a 3.5mm audio jack, a built-in speaker, and a DC power input, along with six physical buttons along one side for power, brightness, contrast, and other functions.
Dasung’s Paperlike 13K has an aluminum alloy body that measures 307 x 241 x 5mm (at its thinnest point) and weighs 721 grams. Dasung doesn’t say how thick the display is at its
thickest
point, but images suggest it’s about twice as thick at the base as it is at the top.
The monitor comes with several accessories including HDMI and USB-C cables, as well as two different stand options. One is a “portable stand stick” that’s pretty much a pen-sized stick that screws into a hole on the back of the monitor, allowing you to prop it up on the go. The other is a magnetic protective cover that serves as a folio case that wraps around the front and back of the display for easy transport, but which can also be folded for use as a stand.
There are also a set of magnetic nuts included in the box that allow you to connect the display to a VESA mount.
A few other things to note:
Dasung only mentions the 300 ppi display resolution for this monitor, but the company is most likely using an E Ink Kaleido 3 display which means that the pixel density will drop to 150 ppi for color content.
E Ink’s Kaleido 3 displays support up to 4096 colors, can be viewed using only ambient light (with no backlight or front light required), and consume very little power because they only need to use electricity when the content on the page is refreshed.
But colors look muted compared with LCD or AMOLED displays, Kaleido screens are typically a little darker than black and white E Ink displays, and while you
can
push screen refresh rates high enough for smooth scrolling, video, and other animations, this typically comes at the cost of visual clarity. So you may notice some ghosting unless you stick to lower refresh rates or occasionally force a full screen refresh.
The color version of this portable monitor does have a front light, but the black and white version does not. So you may want to either count on using it in a well-lit room or investing in a clip-on book light.
The Paperlike 13K doesn’t fully support Apple devices including Macs, iPhones, or iPads yet. Windows, Linux, and Android are.
Orders placed now should ship “in about 3 weeks,” suggesting that we can expect them to ship in mid to late May, 2025.

data.title: Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过技能树（Skill Trees）结构化基于能力课程的新方法，特别适用于计算机科学教育。随着教育向能力导向和自动化教学发展，现有的以理论为中心的课程结构不再适用。技能树展示了技能之间的依赖关系，并结合概念树（Concept Trees）来包含直观的概念或抽象模型。该框架提供了技能树和概念树的正式定义，并给出了设计和课程规划指南。在一个大学数据库课程中的应用显示，学生困惑和压力减少，达到预期技能水平所需的学习时间缩短。本文已提交至Koli Calling '25会议发表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技能树（skill tree）在教育和职业培训中的应用及其潜在问题和优势

不同观点：
• Garlef认为，将技能分解为子技能的方法可能存在教育上的误区。他指出，掌握单独的技能A和B并不意味着能够自动结合起来运用，仍需要额外练习过渡部分。此外，掌握复合技能并不意味着能够单独执行每个部分，因为学习过程中可能是通过过渡学习的。Garlef对总体方法表示兴趣，但认为细节上可能存在偏差。

• Roenxi将该方法与软件工程管理联系起来，指出当前软件管理中存在的胜任力危机，并建议使用基于技能树的能力培训和测试方法。他认为这比现有的依赖指标或超常个体的方法更有效，能够帮助管理人员在特定情况下识别和应对常见问题。

• Didgeroridoo提到Exercism.org已经采用这种方法，并质疑哪些学习领域可能难以应用这种方法。

• Johnecheck支持将技能树用于学习和工作培训，认为这种建模方法很有价值，可以作为学习者的指导地图。他指出大学已经在大范围内使用这种方法，并认为小规模学习也应采用。

• Whiteborb指出，这种方法的“难题”在于需要定义可枚举的“技能”，而现实世界中的技能往往涉及灵活组合工具和策略。不过，他认为这一问题并非不可克服，并提到大型语言模型（LLMs）可能有助于生成新场景。

• Accrual表示支持这种方法，并希望高等教育能采用。他还提到考虑攻读在线硕士学位，质疑其是否采用这种技能树方法。

• Constantcrying强调理论理解在计算机科学教育中的重要性，认为理论理解是帮助理解不同事物如何结合的关键，即使在开发JavaScript web应用时也是如此。

• Cultofmetatron和Johnsutor提到这种方法类似于Math Academy，并认为这种教学模式非常有效，希望更多MOOCs采用。

• Pyinstallwoes联想到游戏中的技能树，如SWG技能树。

• Rahimnathwani提到PDF引用了Justin's book about Math Academy，并建议使用该方法生成技能树，作为LLM提示的一部分，例如生成魔幻现实主义小说写作技能树。

补充讨论：
• 技能树方法在教育和职业培训中的潜在应用和优势，包括其在软件工程管理和在线学习平台中的应用。
• 技能树方法在实际应用中可能面临的挑战，如需要定义和枚举具体技能，以及如何处理现实世界中灵活组合工具和策略的需求。
• 对理论理解在技能培训中的重要性存在不同看法，有人强调理论理解的关键作用，而其他人则更关注技能分解和组合的实用性。
• 不同平台和课程（如Math Academy、Exercism.org）对技能树方法的实际应用及其效果。

Title:
Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees
Authors:
Hildo Bijl
View a PDF of the paper titled Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees, by Hildo Bijl
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Computer science education has seen two important trends. One has been a shift from raw theory towards skills: competency-based teaching. Another has been increasing student numbers, with as a result more automation in teaching. When automating education, it is crucial to properly structure courses, both to manage digitalized educational resources and to facilitate automated coaching algorithms. Currently existing structuring methodologies are focused around theory and not around skills, and are incapable of modeling the dependency links between skills. Because of this, a new didactic framework is needed.
This paper presents a new method of structuring educational contents around skills: something that a student is expected to be able to do. It defines Skill Trees that show dependencies between skills, and subsequently couples these to Concept Trees that contain intuitive ideas/notional machines. Due to the algorithmic nature of computer science, this step-wise approach is especially well-suited to this field of education. Next to formal definitions on Skill Trees and Concept Trees, guidelines are given on how to design them and how to plan a course using them.
The Skill Trees framework has been applied to improve the structure of a university database course. Student interviews indicated reduced confusion/stress and less study time required for students to meet their desired skill level.

data.title: All BART trains were stopped due to ‘computer networking problem’
data.author: ksajadi
data.article_summary: BART服务因电脑网络问题全面暂停，建议乘客选择其他交通方式。Embarcadero站新电梯启用，BART董事会因PG&E停电改至下午1点召开。BART将为2025年Bay to Breakers提供特别早班服务，且在第一季度暴力犯罪率下降23%。2025年初湾区公共交通客流量显著增加。乘客可使用BART行程规划器查看实时信息和站台详情。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BART（旧金山湾区捷运）系统全线停运事件的原因、影响及对公共交通系统的广泛讨论

不同观点：
• **事件原因的猜测与确认**：
  - [scarmig] 猜测停运可能与网络攻击或DNS问题有关，但尚未有确切信息。
  - [kiroguku] 引用了官方声明，指出问题是由于网络设备连接不稳定，导致运营控制中心无法监控列车位置和轨道电路。
  - [noitpmeder] 提到BART总部昨天失去了电力供应，可能与此有关。

• **系统可靠性与技术管理**：
  - [nashashmi] 关注事件后的技术反思和系统改进，质疑是否有政治和技术上的意愿来增强系统韧性。
  - [great_wubwub] 以技术角度调侃，提到在众多评论中没有人提到“生成树环路”问题。

• **公共交通系统的整体问题与比较**：
  - [fhkatari] 指出BART在疫情前进行了扩展，但由于依赖票务收入，受低客流量影响严重。
  - [nashashmi] 提到纽约MTA的机械系统与新系统并行运行导致的延误问题。
  - [ashayh] 对比“较贫穷”国家的公共交通，质疑美国在公共交通上的投资不足，而将大量资金投入AI等领域。

• **乘客体验与设备问题**：
  - [a_t48] 分享了个人经历，表示尽管停运带来了不便，但通过其他交通工具出行体验较好。
  - [CoffeeOnWrite] 抱怨新闸机扫描仪工作不佳，影响乘客通行，且媒体对此问题报道不足。

补充讨论：
• **其他相关信息与讨论**：
  - [satiated_grue] 提到Debian中的一个与PDP-8相关的软件包，虽与事件无关，但引发了技术讨论。
  - [throwaway81523] 和 [jbverschoor] 提到系统因某些故障无法启动，并指出人为操作计算机系统的失误可能是原因之一。
  - [talldatethrow] 认为即使免费，很多人也不会选择乘坐BART，因其脏乱和不安全的问题。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在BART停运事件的原因和技术管理问题上，部分评论质疑官方信息的透明度和技术系统的可靠性。同时，关于公共交通系统的整体投资和乘客体验问题也引发了广泛讨论。

data.title: USPTO refuses Tesla Robotaxi trademark as "merely descriptive"
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 特斯拉计划推出一款售价低于3万美元的无人驾驶双座车，但其商标申请遇阻。美国专利商标局（USPTO）拒绝特斯拉注册“robotaxi”商标，认为该词过于通用，且已有其他公司使用类似名称。此外，特斯拉申请的“Cybercab”商标也被拒，因与其他已注册商标存在潜在混淆。特斯拉必须为车辆寻找新名称，且面临技术挑战，如其自动驾驶系统频需人工干预。特斯拉计划在德州奥斯汀部署这些车辆，但不配备方向盘，将依赖远程操作处理复杂问题。此事还涉及与电影《银翼杀手2049》相关的商标纠纷。
