data.title: Bento gets a makeover
data.author: ordinarily
data.article_summary: Bento是一个开源的云原生数据流处理工具，采用Go语言编写，并作为静态二进制文件部署。它使用声明式配置，支持GCP PubSub、Kafka、NATS、MQTT等多种输入源和Redis、S3、HTTP等输出目标，具备数据映射、多路复用、窗口处理和丰富等功能。Bento简化了数据工程中的常见任务，如数据转换和集成，并支持可测试的配置文件，便于适应需求变化。它还提供广泛的处理器和无状态窗口处理能力，支持自动并行化流工作流。Bento具备可靠的消息处理和无磁盘持久化状态的事务模型，保证至少一次交付。此外，它易于扩展，支持通过Go编写插件或作为子进程运行，并提供指标和追踪功能以增强可观察性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户和开发者对Benthos、Bento、Redpanda及相关开源项目（如Wombat）的现状和发展方向的看法和争议。

不同观点：
• **atombender**：对不同项目活跃度的观察。atombender指出Bento的活跃度远不如Benthos/Redpanda，并提到Wombat项目看起来也像已经停止开发。他认为这些项目的生命力存在差异，并对Bento和Wombat的未来表示怀疑。

• **rekwah**：对项目分叉（forks）持保留态度。rekwah认为虽然分叉代码是可行的，但很难复制原作者的个人风格和品牌形象。他特别提到Benthos的 quirky 营销风格很难被复制，并认为在非原项目上阅读相关文档感觉不够真诚。

• **DidYaWipe**：对Bento项目的改变表示不满。DidYaWipe直接指出当前的Bento已经完全不是原来的项目，并通过一篇博客链接暗示Bento经历了巨大的变化，甚至可能已经失去原有的价值或支持。

补充讨论：
• **项目的活跃度和生命力**：评论中多次提到项目的活跃度问题，特别是Bento和Wombat被认为已经不再活跃或接近死亡，而Redpanda则被视为更具生命力的项目。

• **品牌和风格的复制难度**：rekwah特别提到，除了技术代码本身，项目的品牌和风格也是难以复制的，这成为分叉项目面临的一个挑战。

• **争议焦点**：Bento项目的变化和其与原Benthos项目的关系是争议的焦点。DidYaWipe明显对Bento的改变持批评态度，认为它已经不是原来的项目。

Takes Care of the Dull Stuff
Bento solves common data engineering tasks such as transformations, integrations, and multiplexing with declarative and
unit testable
configuration. This allows you to easily and incrementally adapt your data pipelines as requirements change, letting you focus on the more exciting stuff.
It comes armed with a wide range of
processors
, a
lit mapping language
, stateless
windowed processing capabilities
and an industry leading mascot.
Well Connected
Bento is able to glue a wide range of
sources
and
sinks
together and hook into a variety of
databases
,
caches
,
HTTP APIs
,
lambdas
and
more processors
, enabling you to seamlessly drop it into your existing infrastructure.
Working with disparate APIs and services can be a daunting task, doubly so in a streaming data context. With Bento it's possible to break these tasks down and automatically parallelize them as
a streaming workflow
.
Reliable and Operationally Simple
Delivery guarantees
can be a dodgy subject
. Bento processes and acknowledges messages using an in-process transaction model with no need for any disk persisted state, so when connecting to at-least-once sources and sinks it's able to guarantee at-least-once delivery even in the event of crashes, disk corruption, or other unexpected server faults.
This behaviour is the default and free of caveats, which also makes deploying and scaling Bento much simpler. However, simplicity doesn't negate the need for observability, so it also exposes
metrics
and
tracing
events to targets of your choice.
Extendable
Sometimes the components that come with Bento aren't enough. Luckily, Bento has been designed to be easily plugged with whatever components you need.
You can either write plugins
directly in Go (recommended)
or you can have Bento run your plugin as a
subprocess
.

data.title: RAGDoll: Efficient Offloading-Based Online RAG System on a Single GPU
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为RAGDoll的系统，旨在解决在消费级平台上部署检索增强生成（RAG）时面临的资源限制问题。RAGDoll通过将检索和生成解耦为并行流水线，并结合联合内存分配和动态批调度策略，有效优化了资源利用率。实验表明，RAGDoll能够适应各种硬件配置和大型语言模型规模，相比传统的串行RAG系统，平均延迟速度提升了高达3.6倍。该系统专为资源受限的平台设计，能够在单个GPU上高效运行。

Abstract:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language model (LLM) generation quality by incorporating relevant external knowledge. However, deploying RAG on consumer-grade platforms is challenging due to limited memory and the increasing scale of both models and knowledge bases. In this work, we introduce RAGDoll, a resource-efficient, self-adaptive RAG serving system integrated with LLMs, specifically designed for resource-constrained platforms. RAGDoll exploits the insight that RAG retrieval and LLM generation impose different computational and memory demands, which in a traditional serial workflow result in substantial idle times and poor resource utilization. Based on this insight, RAGDoll decouples retrieval and generation into parallel pipelines, incorporating joint memory placement and dynamic batch scheduling strategies to optimize resource usage across diverse hardware devices and workloads. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RAGDoll adapts effectively to various hardware configurations and LLM scales, achieving up to 3.6 times speedup in average latency compared to serial RAG systems based on vLLM.

43943031.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为RAGDoll的系统，旨在解决在消费级平台上部署检索增强生成（RAG）时面临的资源限制问题。RAGDoll通过将检索和生成解耦为并行流水线，并结合联合内存分配和动态批调度策略，有效优化了资源利用率。实验表明，RAGDoll能够适应各种硬件配置和大型语言模型规模，相比传统的串行RAG系统，平均延迟速度提升了高达3.6倍。该系统专为资源受限的平台设计，能够在单个GPU上高效运行。

data.title: React Three Ecosystem
data.author: bpierre
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：React与三维图形库（如three.js、pixi.js等）的结合及其应用

不同观点：
• [hombre_fatal] 认为React的虚拟DOM（vdom）差异比较机制（diffing）可以很好地应用于像three.js和pixi.js这样的图形库。通过自定义的reconcile函数，可以将命令式的代码（如手动添加、更新物体）转换为声明式的React代码，简化了状态管理和更新过程。这种方法允许开发者以声明式的方式编写代码，而底层库会自动处理复杂的命令式操作。

• [tlarkworthy] 指出three.js本身与React并无直接关联，相关例子展示的是通过流行的React绑定库来使用three.js，这是一种非典型的使用方式。这意味着three.js原生并不支持React，相关功能是通过第三方绑定实现的。

• [talkingtab] 表示作为three.js和React集成的新手，对这些示例感到惊叹，特别是通过React来简化three.js的开发流程，提供了很好的学习与使用体验。

• [cyberax] 提供了另一个例子——React-Native-Skia，展示了类似的虚拟DOM差异比较机制如何应用于不同的状态系统。通过链接和源码展示其实现方式，说明了这种模式在其他图形库中的应用。

• [nawgz] 提出了X3D作为另一种高性能的三维图形技术，并与three.js进行了对比。尽管three.js在社区中更为常见，但nawgz认为X3D在某些方面可能更为强大，尤其是在性能和功能表现上，并对其在浏览器兼容性方面提出了一些疑问。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了React与不同三维图形库（如three.js、React-Native-Skia、X3D）的结合，展示了React如何通过虚拟DOM差异比较机制简化复杂图形应用的开发。
• 争议焦点集中在three.js与X3D的比较上，部分开发者对X3D的较少使用和较高的性能表现感到好奇，并对其在实际项目中的应用潜力提出疑问。

data.title: Radxa Orion O6 brings Arm to the midrange PC (with caveats)
data.author: goranmoomin
data.article_summary: Radxa Orion O6 是一款中端 Arm ITX 主板，具备最高12核CPU、64GB内存和支持Armv9.2，起价略高于200美元。它拥有SystemReady SR认证的BIOS，可运行Windows on Arm和多数Linux arm64系统，但固件存在许多问题，适合喜欢折腾的用户。由于进口关税，美国价格飙升，如32GB型号从400美元涨至1500美元。主板采用CIX CD8180 SoC，配有Arm G720 GPU和30 TOPS NPU，支持高达96GB/s的内存带宽。尽管硬件规格强大，但多核应用表现不如预期，且某些功能可能永远无法实现。尽管未来有望改进，但目前驱动和功能支持仍不完善，特别是在Windows和不同Linux发行版上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新奇硬件供应商不同时投资驱动程序/软件的经济原因及相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **wjnc** 提出疑问，为什么一些新奇硬件供应商不同时投资开发驱动程序和软件。他猜测可能是由于驱动程序的开发会同时惠及当前和未来的竞争对手，因此供应商不愿投资。
• **jasoneckert** 提到进口关税导致硬件价格飙升，使得普通人难以负担硬件，从而影响对软件的开发和实验。他认为这会打击创新，尤其是在美国市场。
• **zettabomb** 分享了自己的使用体验，表示尽管有一些软件和驱动问题，但总体上对产品的性能和价格表示满意，特别是在非美国市场。
• **qwertox** 批评了Radxa在软件支持方面的不足，认为他们依赖社区开发者来完善软件，而Raspberry Pi在这方面做得更好，注重软硬件的平衡。
• **irusensei** 认为关税问题会减少对强大ARM个人电脑或家庭服务器的需求，并指出目前好的选择基本上只有Macs或Ampere。
• **ksec** 讨论了ARM中国的许可问题，推测ARM China可能重新回到了ARM HQ / Softbank的控制之下，并提到了CIX的SoC。
• **solarkraft** 对ARM平台的稳定性和兼容性表示乐观，认为ARM正在从“奇怪的利基平台”转变为“普通的PC”。

补充讨论：
• **zabzonk** 以幽默的方式猜测“Orion Arm”的命名是否与银河系中的猎户臂有关。
• **buyucu** 询问该板的APU是否能与 llama.cpp 兼容，关注具体应用场景的技术可行性。

争议焦点：
• 硬件供应商是否应同时投资软件和驱动程序，社区对此有不同看法。一部分人认为这是必要的投资，另一部分人则认为社区开发者可以填补这一空白。
• 关税对硬件价格的影响及其对软硬件开发的潜在影响也是讨论的重点。

43945041.article_content:
Radxa Orion O6 brings Arm to the midrange PC
...with caveats.
TL;DR
The
Radxa Orion O6
is an Arm ITX motherboard with up to 12 cores, 64 GB of RAM, and Armv9.2 support, starting just over $200 USD
The board has a
SystemReady SR-certified BIOS
, which allows running Windows on Arm and many Linux arm64 ISOs unaltered
The firmware still has many quirks, enough that I wouldn't recommend it if you don't enjoy tinkering with drivers (remember how I said to
temper your expectations
in February?)
Prices for those in the US (like me) just tripled due to import tariffs (ordering the 32 GB model went from $400 to $1500).
The rest of this post is a version of today's video, modified to suit the blog. You can watch the video version below:
Radxa Orion O6
I
pre-ordered
the $300 32GB 'AI kit' the day the Orion O6 was
announced
. And... it never arrived. I'll discuss why at the end of the post, but you may wonder: if it never arrived, how did you review it?
Well, Radxa sent me a
16 gig
version of board
for testing and review. I always disclose when something is provided, so I'm disclosing that here. See
all my sponsorship and review policies on GitHub
.
They sent a 16 GB kit to many hardware testers and reviewers, and for
months
, we've had what Radxa calls a
debug party
. People post their issues, and hopefully Radxa fixes some of those things before the public launch.
Except, the public launch
already happened
, and there are still
fundamental
problems with the board. I'll talk about those after I walk through the hardware.
Hardware
In the box, you get the O6 board itself, with a heatsink/cooler combo. It also has an acrylic case that looks nice and provides adequate ventilation, though it gets in the way of PCIe card brackets, if you don't remove them.
It's powered by a soldered-on CIX CD8180 SoC, with the following specs:
Armv9.2
12 CPU cores (4x 'big' A720 at 2.6 GHz, 4x 'medium' A720 at 2.4 GHz, 4x 'little' A520 at 1.8 GHz)
12MB L3 shared cache
Arm Immortals G720 MC10 GPU
Cix 30 TOPS NPU
The CPU is backed by up to 64GB of LPDDR5 RAM, with a 128 bit bus. This means memory bandwidth can get 'up to 96 GB/s' (though in reality, for
CPU
tasks, I measured up to 40-50 GB/s).
For IO, though, this is the most fully-featured Arm board outside of server-class boards from Ampere:
2x USB-C ports for both PD and even DisplayPort. The first port can do 4K60 output.
2x USB 2.0 Type A / 2x USB 3.2 Type A
HDMI (up to 4K60)
DisplayPort (up to 4K120)
Dual 5 Gbps Ethernet (RTL8126)
Headset jack
On the surface of the board, there are front panel IO and audio headers, power input via either USB-C PD (65W recommended) or 24-pin ATX header.
There's also a lot of PCIe Gen 4 lanes exposed:
M.2 M-key (up to 2280 size) Gen 4 with 4 lanes
M.2 E-key (2230 size) Gen 4 with 2 lanes
PCIe x16 slot, Gen 4 with 8 lanes
My
favorite
part is the full-size PCI Express slot, which Radxa forum user
willy pushed to its limit with 100 Gbps networking
. He was able to get 70 gigabits of traffic through HAproxy, meaning this board
could
be a quiet networking beast.
Could
be, because as I've found, there's also a
lot
of weirdness around how the CPU works, that prevents most multi-core apps from running as fast as they
should
.
Bringup
And anyone who's bought Radxa hardware early on knows this, but it bears mentioning: this board needs a little more time in the oven.
Radxa has a
docs site with a lot of helpful information
. The board runs a lot of things well already. But if you already ordered one of these things, don't expect all the features on their website to run day-one.
Some things, don't expect them to
ever
run. In fact, when I pre-ordered my 32 GB board, the website said there were
12 cores at up to 2.8 Gigahertz
. As of today, the specs were updated to showing 12 cores, but 'up to 2.6 gigahertz'.
And in reality, with the latest firmware, depending on how you're running the board, you might only get
8
cores. And only 2.4 or 2.5 gigahertz.
But in positive news, the firmware that limits the board to 8 cores is SystemReady SR certified, meaning it has full UEFI support and can run Windows or Linux arm64 natively.
That
doesn't
mean everything works out of the box though. If you want run Windows, there are still
precious few drivers
for Windows on Arm. And on Linux, depending on what version and what distro you install, you might or might not get support for features like the iGPU, or the 5 Gbps Ethernet. Each of the major distros I tested was lacking one feature or another.
In a year or two, the Orion O6 will be in a better place. I probably spent a dozen hours just working on different driver issues to test everything. That's not something I'd want you to have to do, too.
Benchmarking
After not one but
two
full cycles of testing, first on a 0.2.x firmware, then again on the SystemReady firmware at version 9,
I have test data
.
A lot of it
.
I've said before, what I'm looking for is basically Apple's M-series performance and efficiency, but in a more open plat

data.author: dave1629
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google的市场垄断与创新影响

不同观点：
• **支持分离搜索索引**：Snielson和部分评论者支持Kagi的提议，将Google的搜索索引与其他服务分离。他们认为这样可以增加市场竞争，并减少Google对市场的主导控制。Kagi的博客进一步解释了这一观点。

• **Google推动AI创新的贡献**：Bloppe和部分评论者认为，Google在推动AI技术发展方面做出了巨大贡献，包括资助基础研究和开发Transformer架构。如果削弱Google的资源和能力，可能会对整体创新产生负面影响。

• **反垄断行动的负面影响**：Beambot和一些评论者担心，针对Google的反垄断行动可能会对整个科技 startup 生态系统产生不利影响，尤其是在IPO窗口关闭的情况下，可能导致M&A活动冻结，影响创业公司的退出机制。

• **Google的垄断地位影响市场公平**：Light_triad和部分评论者认为，Google通过垄断分发渠道，对市场造成了不公平的竞争环境。创业公司需要通过Google的“收费站”才能接触到市场，这对创业公司来说是一个巨大的负担。

• **YC的双重标准**：Workaccount2批评YC一方面受益于将创业公司出售给Google，另一方面却反对Google的创新活动，认为YC只是希望Google购买他们的产品而不是自行开发。

• **政府资助与垄断**：Bender提出，是否可以比较各搜索引擎在创建和运营过程中获得的政府资助，以更全面地评估其市场地位。

• **AI行业的竞争性**：Xiphias2认为，AI行业本身是非常竞争和健康的，拥有搜索索引并不是决定性优势，数据并不是关键因素。

• **Google的历史贡献与当前垄断问题**：Creato认为，Google过去提供了许多优秀的产品和服务，但当前的垄断问题确实存在，不能简单地将Google的成功归因于垄断行为。

data.title: The deathbed fallacy
data.author: mefengl
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了所谓的“临终谬误”（Deathbed Fallacy）。许多人临终时常常后悔没有多陪伴家人、多旅行、少担忧等，这些遗憾被广泛传播并用于人生建议。然而，作者认为，临终者的 regret 并不能作为当前生活决策的可靠指南。原因有三：

1. **非代表性状态**：临终时的心态无法代表整个人生的幸福或意义，临终者没有未来，他们的想法仅限于当下和记忆。
2. **不了解过去的自己**：人们往往以为自己了解过去的自己，但实际上记忆和认知存在偏差，导致对过去决策的误解。
3. **近因效应**：临终者的遗憾可能受到老年阶段的记忆影响，而非整个人生的全面反思。

作者强调，不应单纯依赖临终者的遗憾来指导当前生活，因为每个时间点的自己都是不同的“人”，临终时的看法未必明智。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于临终遗憾的观点及其合理性

不同观点：
• **lolinder**：认为作者过于关注“临终遗憾”这一现代概念，而忽视了这一思想在多种文化和历史中的普遍存在。他引用了马可·奥勒留、道德经、佛教的念死概念、古兰经和圣经中的例子，说明反思死亡并据此调整生活是人类普遍的现象。

• **bombcar**：认为“临终遗憾”是一种修辞手法，用来审视自己的生活，确定真正的目标，并提出难以面对的问题，以此激励自我反思。

• **gus_massa**：质疑临终遗憾列表的选择性，指出除非有对临终时刻的记录和统计，否则这些列表可能只是基于不可靠的记忆，缺乏准确性。

• **roenxi**：认为文章虽然准确，但忽视了有些人即使在临终时仍有重大错误和遗憾，因此不能简单地依赖临终者的建议，而应从那些认为自己生活圆满的人身上学习。

补充讨论：
- 临终遗憾的普遍性和文化背景。

43944467.article_content:
“Lord Byron on his Death-bed” by Joseph Denis Odevaere
This topic has bothered me for years. So now, in a moment of inspiration instigated by
Wait But Why
1
and drinking a glass or two of bourbon, I want to hash it out. It is something I call
the Deathbed Fallacy
.
What is the Deathbed Fallacy?
People on their deathbeds regret not spending more time of their life with their family, traveling more, worrying less, etc. I’ve heard this truism echoed by
growth gurus
and spiritualists. It
is
amplified
by
newspapers
. It comes up at dinner discussions. The origin the list of regrets is the palliative nurse
Bronnie Ware
who listed the following most common regrets:
“I wish I’d had the courage to live a life true to myself, not the life others expected of me.
I wish I didn’t work so hard.
I wish I’d had the courage to express my feelings.
I wish I had stayed in touch with my friends.
I wish that I had let myself be happier.”
All well and good. A bit vague, but seems like solid advice. So what is the
problem?
The Fallacy
The fallacy is to assume that whoever you are on your deathbed knows how you should live your life right now. They wish they would have done things differently, meaning, they think
you
should do something differently,
right now
. You should consider yourself over a lifetime not as a single person, but a line of many people with different views and priorities. Now, do you think the last person in that line is wise and all-knowing? There are three reasons to doubt that deathbed-you is a competent guide for your life.
The deathbed you is not a reliable advisor. Here’s why.
Reason 1: It is not a representative state
The deathbed is not a representative state of life, and what you want when you
are there might not have much correlation with what would have been the happiest, most satisfactory and/or meaningful life you could have led.
The deathbed you is very special in a few ways:
They don’t have a future at all. They are about to die, and nothing they
think has a bearing on the future. All they have is the present and memories.
They think they know their past selves (such as you) very well but probably
don’t. More on that soon.
Like all your temporal selves, they are locked in a time, place and life
situation that does not necessarily correspond to yours.
We should also expect recency bias to play a significant role. We should assume that the people expressing these regrets are in general quite old. Their memories of working a lot should be dominated by the late stages of their careers. The lost friends should be those they miss at old age, not necessarily the people you hung out with in your twenties that you’ve forgotten almost entirely by the time you’re 60.
Reason 2: You don’t know your past selves, but you think you do
The older I get, the more I think I understand myself as a teenager. As I learn more about myself, I seem to grasp my motivations and my core ides ever more fully. So I tend to think of past me as
nothing but a slightly less grown-up, more athletic version of myself
. I think I’ve been consistent. And when I made the “wrong” choices, it’s either because I was (am) stupid, or because I didn’t have the right information.
But every now and then I find something I wrote or remember a decision I made in high school, which reminds me that my assumptions are all wrong. I was just as smart in high school, I had a lot of information (more than I do now because I’ve forgotten the details). The decisions I made were actually the right ones, and what I think now is wrong, because present me is overly simplistic about past me.
Case in point: for a few years, when I was 14 to 15, a big priority in my life was fitting in, and not be too open about my own ideas and feelings. This goes entirely against both my current ideals and the Deathbed List. So young me would have benefitted from some guidance from present me, right?
Wrong. When I find a diary from that time or talk to a friend from those days about it, it turns out I was probably doing the right thing. My core values were the same as now, only somewhat more 2-dimensional. I valued independence and authenticity back then, too. But what younger me realized, that present me forgot, was that I
sucked
as a person in a lot of ways and that people, in general, weren’t very fond of me. I also realized that no matter how enlightened or authentic I got, my overall happiness depended quite a lot on how other people saw me, and what relationship we developed.
Today, I probably care too much about what others think. I often blame teenage me for making me so aware of other people’s judgment – why can’t I just focus on cool work and meditation all the time with a select few people I love? But that is just present me shaming past me for dragging himself through an ordeal which benefitted us both. He handled the most pressing matter and passed on the work of undoing the side-effects to me. I just forgot about it and got stuck in regret.

data.title: Embracer Games Archive is preserving 75000 video games and needs contributions
data.author: draugadrotten
data.article_summary: Embracer Games Archive旨在保存和记录电子游戏历史，目前收藏了超过75,000件游戏、主机和配件，但仍在不断扩展中。他们的目标是建立一个尽可能全面的实体游戏档案，并最终在网站上分享数据库。档案馆特别寻找一些特定平台的大型收藏，如3DO、Amstrad CPC 464和Apple II等，同时也对巴西、韩国和台湾的游戏感兴趣。他们欢迎出售或捐赠，并乐意与研究机构和行业伙伴合作。虽然档案馆不对公众开放，但通过网站和社交媒体提供内部工作的 insight。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Embracer Games Archive的开放性、目的及其对公众的价值。

不同观点：
• [mzajc] 认为该档案馆虽然声称对所有人开放，但实际优先考虑支持游戏文化、历史和行业的请求，且不对公众开放，感觉像是单向的付出，没有回馈社会。相比之下，支持像GOG.com和Internet Archive这样真正向公众开放的平台更有意义。

• [forgotTheLast] 指出Embracer Group曾购买多个游戏 franchise 的IP并终止其开发，质疑其目的的正当性，认为具有讽刺意味。

• [pogue] 提到档案馆寻求的是游戏贡献而非金钱捐赠，但对档案馆的具体用途缺乏明确说明，仅提到用于研究和可能的博物馆展示。

• [zabzonk] 对Embracer Group及其子公司的背景表示困惑，认为其身份不明确。

• [jll29] 建议至少部分收藏应作为公共展览，通过收取门票费用来增加公众 awareness 和支持，而不是完全封闭。

• [nrb] 持 cynical 观点，怀疑Embracer 建立档案馆的目的是利用公众捐赠的游戏来训练AI。

• [biglyburrito] 表示不信任Embracer Group能有效管理游戏档案。

• [integricho] 质疑公众能从Embracer Games Archive中获得什么实际利益。

• [merbanan] 指出档案馆似乎没有对媒体进行数字化处理。

• [devwastaken] 认为实体档案馆效率低下且成本高昂，最终可能被废弃；主张数字化的档案如torrent seeding才是最好的方式。

补充讨论：
• 对Embracer Group及其动机的广泛不信任，部分评论对其历史行为持批评态度。
• 公众对档案馆开放性和透明度的关注，尤其是对档案馆具体用途和公众回馈的质疑。
• 对实体档案馆的实用性和长期可行性的讨论，一些评论支持数字化解决方案。

The development of our archive is still in its early stages on an ongoing journey. Even though we currently have around 75,000 items in the archive, we are far from having every video game, accessory, and gaming system in existence.
Our goal for the future is to share our database here on the website, allowing everyone to see what is in the archive.
If you have something you’d like to sell or donate, please feel free to contact our Acquisitions Manager, Thomas Sunhede, at
[email protected]
.
Thanks!
Right now we are especially searching for big collections of:
3DO
Amstrad CPC 464
Apple II
Bandai Playdia
BBC Micro
Dragon 32
Macintosh big box
MSX
PC big box
Philips CD-i
Also of interest:
Brazilian games, South Korean games, Taiwanese games
For us at Embracer Games Archive, games are an important part of our shared history. Games are works of art that have influenced and inspired people and culture over the past decades. Our ambition is to be a small part of the greater work being done to preserve gaming history through our archive of physical games.
The inspiration for the archive originated from Embracer's CEO, Lars Wingefors, a seasoned professional in the gaming industry and a private collector himself. As both the game collection and the Embracer Group expanded, the concept emerged to establish an archive that would imbue the games within the collection with a more profound significance.
Being a patron of video games history, the goal of the archive is to be a part of the community that preserves and documents games history by collaborating with institutions, grass root movements, journalists, researchers, publishers and studios – not only for the Embracer group but for the whole industry. By doing so we promote and help build the heritage of games which is something that will benefit the entire games industry in the long run..
What is the purpose of the archive?
plus-minus
Our mission is to have an archive of physical games as extensive as possible. With the purpose of contributing to the joint preservation of video game culture and history.
Is it video games for all formats/consoles/computer?
plus-minus
Basically yes, we are seeking games, consoles, computers, and accessories released for the consumer market.
Will you be able to do research in the archive?
plus-minus
We are happy to collaborate with initiatives to preserve and document games. If you have an inquiry please do not hesitate to contact us.
How many games do you have in the archive?
plus-minus
At the moment the archive contains over 75,000 games, consoles, and accessories.
Where is the archive based?
plus-minus
Karlstad, Sweden.
Can I visit the archive?
plus-minus
The archive is for everyone, and we welcome all inquiries. However, we prioritize requests that support gaming culture, gaming history, and the games industry. For example, we aim to assist and grant access to people within the games industry, researchers, schools, and other institutions. data.title: The cult of doing business
data.author: Caiero
data.article_summary: 《The Cult of Doing Business》一文回顾了企业家工作伦理的演变，作者Erik Baker探讨了创业文化如何塑造现代工作观念。文章指出，自工业革命以来，企业家精神被赋予了极高的价值，尤其在科技和创新领域。这种文化推崇长时间工作、风险承担和自我牺牲，逐渐形成了所谓的“创业崇拜”。然而，这种工作伦理也引发了对劳工权益和生活质量的担忧。Baker分析了这种现象的历史根源及其对当代社会的影响，呼吁在追求效率和创新的同时，关注劳动者的福祉和平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于现代社会中工作、盈余和信仰危机的讨论，以及对技术崇拜、商业文化、工作伦理等方面的不同看法。

不同观点：
• jmogly认为，当前的危机是信仰危机，源于人类在农业和畜牧业发展后产生的盈余，导致人们不断构建各种系统来填补内心的空虚。这种盈余引发了无意义的追求，形成了一种崇拜盈余的文化，通过技术进步或剥削等方式来获取更多盈余，但这种存在是空洞的。真正的道路是利用盈余来拥抱我们精神中的积极方面。

• simpaticoder通过评论小说《Cryptonomicon》指出，书中的技术企业家视角是一种无心、机械的世界观，强调对知识的追求而非情感或人性，反映了现代商业文化中深层的狂妄和道德风险。

• djoldman认为，现代西方经济中的利润越来越多地依赖于对人类缺陷的剥削，例如通过戏剧性和负面内容吸引注意力，或利用人类对归属感的需求进行剥削。同时，监管俘获和利用监管漏洞也是重要问题。

• moshegramovsky指出，许多人通过操纵策略来获取他们想要的东西，但当这些策略失败时，他们的真实面目就显露出来了。他强调真诚的重要性，并分享了自己与一位真诚且公平的老板的积极经历。

• mlsu认为，保持真诚的关系是关键，工作、家庭和休闲是生活的三大支柱。他反对欺骗和操纵，认为这些才是真正有害的。

• foobarbecue质疑评论模式，认为这些评论更像是书评而非原创文章，并提出评论的目的是帮助决定是否购买书籍。

• ashoeafoot将商业的无控制扩展比喻为自然界的生态破坏，认为崇拜这种商业文化只是重新包装的自然崇拜。

• greenie_beans将现代商业文化描述为“微封建主义”，结合了技术封建主义和微名人的概念。

• rubitxxx强调爱本身是最重要的工作，引用了马斯洛的需求层次理论来支持这一观点。

• know-how反驳了将爱视为最重要的工作的观点，指出实际生活中需要用金钱支付账单。

• bgnn认为，对财富积累的痴迷并非美国独有，但在美国个体中更为普遍接受。

• bix6对文章的建议部分不足表示遗憾。

• dade_提到新教工作伦理，认为这是对当前问题的传统解释，不需要新的解释。

• ChrisMarshallNY指出，对职业的奉献并非美国独有，例如日本对工作的严肃态度。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了对现代商业文化的批判，特别是对技术崇拜和商业剥削的讨论。
• 有对真诚和公平领导方式的赞赏，与操纵和剥削形成对比。
• 提到了不同文化和背景下的工作伦理和信仰差异，如美国与日本的对比。
• 对书籍《Cryptonomicon》的评论引发了对现代技术企业家视角的深入讨论。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否应将爱视为最重要的工作，存在不同看法。
• 对现代商业文化的本质和影响有不同解读，一些人认为其本质是剥削和空洞的，另一些人则认为这是不可避免的经济现象。

data.article_summary: "Visiones cuánticas"是一个结合艺术、科学、技术的展览，将于2025年2月21日至6月8日在展览馆展出。展览期间将举办多场活动，包括由Jaime de los Ríos主持的导览参观、与物理学家Rainer Blatt和电影制作人Jaione Camborda的对话、以及艺术工作坊等。此外，还有关于量子计算和量子理论的讨论，如"Quantum Computing for 0€"和"On how matter is noisy"。展览还提供多个开放征集项目，如2025年艺术项目开发的工作室资源征集和国际交流驻留计划。展览免费开放，并有多种语言选择（EU、ES、EN）。

data.title: QueryLeaf: SQL for Mongo
data.author: tilt
data.article_summary: QueryLeaf 是一个可以将 SQL 查询转换为 MongoDB 命令的库，适用于 Node.js 环境。它使用 `node-sql-parser` 解析 SQL 查询，并将其转换为 MongoDB 命令，通过 MongoDB 官方驱动执行。该库支持基本的 SQL 操作（SELECT、INSERT、UPDATE、DELETE）以及高级功能如嵌套字段访问、数组元素访问、聚合查询（GROUP BY）、集合间的 JOIN 操作等。它提供了多种接口，包括直接集成到代码中的库、命令行工具（CLI）、Web 服务器（REST API）和 PostgreSQL Wire Protocol Server。用户可以通过 `npm install @queryleaf/lib` 安装并使用该库，并结合 MongoDB 客户端执行 SQL 查询。此外，还提供了 `DummyQueryLeaf` 用于无数据库连接的测试和调试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将Mongo与SQL结合的技术方案及其可行性、性能和使用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **ttfkam** 对Mongo支持SQL的性能持怀疑态度，认为只有在最简单的情况下才可能具有性能优势。他提到Postgres的jsonb索引使得反过来（即在关系数据库中处理JSON数据）更可行。

• **sparky_** 对这种技术方案的实际应用场景感到困惑，认为如果数据本质上是关系的，就应该使用关系型数据库存储；如果不是，强行将其关系化可能会带来性能问题。

• **gavinray** 提供了一个具体的解决方案，提到AWS的JDBC驱动支持DocumentDB与Mongo，允许用户像操作常规SQL JDBC数据库一样操作Mongo。

• **gitroom** 对Mongo和SQL的结合感到困惑，表示更习惯使用Postgres和jsonb。同时提出了Postgres在扩展性方面的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **性能与可行性争议**：ttfkam和sparky_对Mongo支持SQL的性能和应用场景存在质疑，ttfkam更看好Postgres的jsonb索引。

• **技术实现与工具**：gavinray提供了一个实际的技术工具（AWS JDBC驱动），展示了如何在实践中实现Mongo与SQL的结合。

• **扩展性问题**：gitroom提出了Postgres在扩展性方面的实际问题，暗示尽管其在处理JSON数据上具有优势，但在扩展性上可能仍存在挑战。

争议焦点：Mongo与SQL结合的技术方案在实际应用中的性能表现和使用场景的合理性。

QueryLeaf
SQL to MongoDB query translator for NodeJS
Overview
QueryLeaf is a library that translates SQL queries into MongoDB commands. It parses SQL using node-sql-parser, transforms it into an abstract command set, and then executes those commands against the MongoDB Node.js driver.
Features
Parse SQL statements into an abstract syntax tree using node-sql-parser
Compile SQL AST into MongoDB commands
Execute MongoDB commands using the official driver
Support for basic SQL operations:
SELECT
INSERT
UPDATE
DELETE
Advanced querying features:
Nested field access (e.g.,
address.zip
)
Array element access (e.g.,
items[0].name
)
GROUP BY with aggregation functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX)
JOINs between collections
Multiple interfaces:
Library for direct integration in your code
CLI for command-line SQL queries
Web Server for REST API access
PostgreSQL Wire Protocol Server
for connecting with standard PostgreSQL clients

The Sun May Be Entering an Era of Stronger 11-Year Cycles
The sun has produced stunning auroras on Earth in recent years as solar activity has peaked—but expect more in coming years
By
Meghan Bartels
edited by
Dean Visser
Massive solar flares, graceful eruptions of solar material, and an enormous sunspot make up some of the imagery captured by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory in 2013 and 2014.
NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center/SDO/S. Wiessinger
A year ago this weekend, the sun’s activity created
some of the most spectacular auroras on record
, with displays visible as far south as Florida.
The incredible spectacles last May (and another auroral outburst last October) were partly a matter of luck because several factors, some of them serendipitous, affect the appearance of aurora. But the sun had been primed to put on a show as it approached the
maximum phase of its 11-year activity cycle
—and that high activity continues today. This solar cycle still has the potential to cause more celestial spectacles before activity calms down. And scientists say that the coming solar cycles may be even more eventful. But it remains quite difficult to predict the sun’s behavior.
“Solar storms—it’s a probabilistic thing, so sometimes they don’t always do what you would expect,” says Lisa Upton, a heliophysicist at the Southwest Research Institute.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
The Sun Right Now
The sun is essentially a massive liquid magnet. Heliophysicists gauge our star’s activity by tallying
the number of sunspots
—relatively “cold” knots of its magnetic field that are often the source of radiation and plasma outbursts—on its surface. (Scientists monitor this tally in real time, but they evaluate the solar cycle’s stages based on smoothed averages over many months. So the formal declaration of a cycle’s solar maximum and minimum always happens after the fact.)
The number of sunspots naturally rises and falls over about 11 years, during which the
sun’s magnetic poles first strengthen, then weaken and finally flip
. When the sun’s magnetic field is calmest—with one pole that is firmly positive and one that is firmly negative—activity is at its minimum, as it was most recently around December 2019, and the star is sometimes entirely free of blemishes.
For more than a year now, the sun has been in the opposite phase—the solar maximum—with a messy magnetic field, plenty of sunspots and regular outbursts. August 2024 produced the most sunspots of any recent month, with more than 200 such storms.
Sunspots have since become less numerous, but it’s still unclear whether the solar maximum is truly on its way out. “We’ve had a little bit of a slowdown in activity [during] the last couple months. That’s not too surprising,” Upton says. “A question at this point, which will be interesting, is whether or not we’re going to have another little spike in activity.”
She says that if such a spike were to happen, it would likely come within about three months, mirroring a small spike that occurred in June and July 2023. “But the sun likes to surprise us,” Upton adds, “so we’ll see if that happens.”
Long-Term Cycles
Even as scientists watch the current solar cycle unfold, they’re also working to understand what future cycles might bring.
That’s a difficult task, given that modern science is only in the 25th activity cycle in which researchers have made plentiful sunspot observations. More sophisticated observations that help scientists understand the sun in detail, such as space-based observations and magnetic data, are even newer, with some offering insight into only a couple of solar cycles thus far. Scientists can study
tree rings and ice cores to get a basic sense of solar activity before observations began
, but these data are less detailed and don’t provide precise sunspot counts.
One hypothesis suggests that the sun displays a longer-term variability called the Gleissberg cycle, named for astronomer Wolfgang Gleissberg, who posited such 80-year cycles in the 1960s. (Other proposed
longer-duration cycles in solar behavior
include the Suess–de Vries cycle, lasting 195 to 235 years, and the Hallstatt cycle, stretching over some 2,400 years.) And a new analysis of protons trapped in the inner radiation belt that surrounds Earth
suggests a new Gleissberg cycle may be beginning
.
Not all heliophysicists are sold on the Gleissberg cycle, however, given the scant data scientists have to work with. “It’s kind of debatable whether or not this is a physical phenomenon versus a statistical phenomenon,” Upton says.
Regardless, chances are good that during the coming solar cycles, the sun will be more active than it has been over the past two decades. That’s because Solar Cycle 24,

data.title: Fixrleak: Fixing Java Resource Leaks with GenAI
data.author: benocodes
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种名为FixrLeak的生成式AI框架，用于自动检测和修复Java应用程序中的资源泄漏问题。资源泄漏会导致性能下降和系统故障，传统上通过手动或早期自动化工具进行修复，但这些方法存在耗时、易出错和难以扩展等问题。FixrLeak结合抽象语法树（AST）分析和生成式AI，根据Java最佳实践（如try-with-resources）生成准确且符合惯用法的修复方案。其架构包括输入收集、AST分析和提示工程等步骤，已在Uber的大规模Java代码库中显著减少了手动工作量，提高了开发效率和代码质量。FixrLeak在处理可轻松修复的泄漏时具有高准确性，适用于工业级资源泄漏管理。

Introduction
Resource leaks, where resources like files, database connections, or streams aren’t properly released after use, are a persistent issue in Java applications. These leaks can lead to performance degradation,  and system failures. While tools like SonarSource SonarQube
™
effectively identify such leaks, the fixing process remains manual, time-consuming, and prone to errors. To address this, we developed FixrLeak, a generative AI-based framework that automates the detection and repair of resource leaks. FixrLeak combines Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis with generative AI (GenAI) to produce accurate, idiomatic fixes while following Java best practices like try-with-resources. Deployed within Uber’s extensive Java codebase, FixrLeak significantly reduces manual effort, improves developer productivity, and improves code quality, showcasing the transformative potential of AI-driven solutions in large-scale software engineering.
Background
Understanding Resource Leaks in Java
Resource leaks occur when a program fails to properly release resources such as files, database connections, or streams after use. These leaks can lead to serious issues, including performance degradation, application failures, and an inability to handle additional operations due to resource exhaustion. For example, if a file descriptor isn’t released quickly, it could prevent an application from opening new files, ultimately causing system instability.
Consider the example below, where a BufferedReader object is used to read from a file. In the original code (Figure 1), the reader isn’t closed properly, resulting in a resource leak. Historically, developers relied on try/catch/finally blocks to handle such cases, but missing or incorrect finally blocks often led to leaks. Modern Java best practices recommend the try-with-resources statement, which significantly reduces boilerplate code and ensures resources are released safely, even if exceptions occur during execution.
Figure 1: Original code with a resource leak.
Figure 2: Fixed Code using
try-with-resources
.
In the revised version (Figure 2) the
BufferedReader
is declared within the try block using the
try-with-resources
statement, ensuring that it’s automatically closed when no longer needed. This practice simplifies the code and eliminates the risk of resource leaks, making it an essential technique for modern Java programming.
Tackling Resource Leaks: What Came Before FixrLeak
Before FixrLeak, resource leak fixes were either manual or handled by early automated tools.
RLFixer
, a non-GenAI tool, relied on pre-designed templates and analysis frameworks like
WALA
. While effective for some leaks, these tools struggled to scale in massive codebases like Uber’s and required extensive manual setup for each new programming idiom.
GenAI-based solutions, like
InferFix
, moved the needle by using large language models to automate fixes. However, InferFix had its limitations, including only 70% fix accuracy and challenges with complex leaks requiring advanced code analysis. Additionally, it relied on proprietary models that couldn’t easily adapt to evolving technologies.
FixrLeak builds on these lessons, using generative AI in a scalable, template-free approach that works seamlessly across Uber’s codebase. It focuses on easily fixable leaks to achieve higher accuracy, making it a game-changer for industrial-scale resource leak management.
Architecture
Figure 3: Resource leak-fixing workflow with Fixrleak.
The general flow of FixrLeak is shown in Figure 3. We currently focus on fixing leaks where the lifetime of the resource doesn’t exceed the function that allocated the resource.
Input Gathering
FixrLeak starts by scanning resource leaks reported by SonarQube, gathering key details like file names and line numbers. To account for changes in the codebase, it uses a deterministic hash based on the file and function name, ensuring accurate tracking of leaks and their fixes. Once identified, FixrLeak uses the
Tree-sitter
library to parse the code and extract the relevant function for analysis.
AST-Level Analysis
Fixing resource leaks isn’t always straightforward—blindly applying fixes can lead to new issues, like use-after-close errors. For example, if a resource like a
BufferedReader
is returned from a method, closing it prematurely could break the code at its caller site. To avoid such pitfalls, FixrLeak uses Tree-sitter to perform AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) analysis.
This analysis ensures that FixrLeak skips functions where resources are passed as parameters, returned, or stored in fields, as these resources often outlive the function’s scope. By focusing only on safe-to-fix scenarios, FixrLeak delivers precise, reliable fixes while leaving more complex cases for advanced analysis at the caller level.

try-with-resources
within the function.

fastgron transforms JSON into discrete assignments to make it easier to grep for what you want and see the absolute 'path' to it. It eases the exploration of APIs that return large blobs of JSON but have terrible documentation.

主要讨论点：对鸡蛋价格上涨及相关供应链和企业利润的分析与质疑

不同观点：
• **floundy** 认为文章作者缺乏经济学专业知识，单凭鸡蛋零售价格上涨不能证明供应商在剥削消费者。他指出，需要调查零售商的利润空间，才能确定供应链中是否有人通过操纵叙事获取超额利润。他还质疑文章选择使用损益表（P/L）而非毛收入作为证据，认为这不足以证明作者的论点，暗示文章可能有政治动机。

• **tzs** 提出文章中提到Cal-Maine公司的利润比去年同期增长了四倍，但在页面底部推荐的其他文章中，有一篇提到Cal-Maine的季度财报未达到华尔街预期，导致股价下跌。他对此表示好奇，质疑华尔街是否预期利润增长应更高。

• **njdas** 认为在没有更多证据的情况下，很难判断是否存在不当行为，并提到司法部可能会在未来找到证据。他指出Cal-Maine的利润存在波动，并提到公司将支付创纪录的3.13亿美元税款，显示其收入情况。

• **superkuh** 建议阅读Cory Doctorow的文章，该文章早在几个月前就揭露了类似问题。他批评《华尔街日报》的文章链接难以阅读，技术实现上不如其他文章链接友好。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到Cal-Maine公司的财务数据，如净利润和税款支付，这些数据被用来分析公司利润的真实情况。
• 争议的焦点在于鸡蛋价格上涨的原因及供应链中各方的角色，特别是零售商和供应商是否存在剥削行为或操纵利润的情况。

43945116.article_content:
(Image credit: Huawei)
Yesterday, Huawei
unveiled
its Matebook Pro 2025 laptops, powered by HarmonyOS, the firm's newly developed operating system, independent of Linux and Android, breaking free from
Microsoft
's shackles. At the event, Chinese enthusiasts had a go with the machine. They discovered it reportedly features a new SoC from Huawei's chip subsidiary HiSilicon, the
Kirin X90
, built on a custom Arm-based design. This might be Huawei's "Apple silicon" moment, integrating its devices with in-house software and hardware, though compatibility with already-developed applications remains an open question.
Following sanctions imposed in 2020, the US significantly limited Huawei in its ability to work with international chip designers and manufacturers. Within a short span, the firm was forced to rely on indigenous alternatives, sourcing chips from its HiSilicon division, with manufacturing primarily handled by China's SMIC. Unlike
Loongson's chips
, which employ its custom LoongArch architecture, Huawei's cores utilize off-the-shelf Arm Cortex designs, and now its own Arm-based Taishan V-series architectures.
Huawei's laptops have mostly been powered by hardware from AMD/Intel, with
a few exceptions
. While Huawei showcased its upcoming HarmonyOS-powered Matebook Pro laptops, enthusiasts found evidence that the Kirin X90 SoC powers them through the system information. Further details by leaker Digital Chat Station suggest the Kirin X90, codenamed Charlotte Pro, wields a 10-core (4+4+2) / 20-thread layout.
The design is said to mirror the
Kirin 9010
, found on Huawei's Pura 70 series mobile phones. Therefore, the four prime cores will likely utilize the Taishan V121 architecture. In contrast, the performance cores step down to Taishan V120, and the efficiency cores probably use a standard Cortex design, likely the Cortex-A510.
Kirin X90 https://t.co/olAhXrC6NW pic.twitter.com/QMM3zuTKWD
May 9, 2025
There aren't many performance indicators yet, but server-oriented designs, likely the Kunpeng 930, of the
Taishan V120
architecture, match AMD's
Zen 3
in single-core performance. The Kirin X90 will still probably be built using SMIC's aging 7nm process node, which is the likely bottleneck. Having their own OS and silicon makes Huawei less dependent on Western tech. It ensures tighter integration within its ecosystem, leading to better optimization, reliability, faster development, and performance.
So, how many developers will port their existing apps to
HarmonyOS
? That depends on how well the platform takes off. Compatibility layers are a solution, but in the end, if Huawei wants a bite of Apple's market share, it needs a strong ecosystem, including essential daily apps. That being said, building homegrown software alternatives is also an option that fits China's ambitions of tech autarky. No matter what, we can expect to see some actual performance tests of the chip once the Matebook Pro comes out on May 19.

data.title: EM-LLM: Human-Inspired Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs
data.author: jbotz
data.article_summary: EM-LLM是一种受人类情景记忆启发的大语言模型架构，能够在不微调的情况下处理几乎无限长度的上下文，同时保持计算效率。该模型通过结合贝叶斯 surprise 和图论边界优化将输入序列组织成连贯的情景事件，并在需要时通过基于相似性和时间连续性的两阶段记忆过程进行检索。实验表明，EM-LLM在LongBench和∞-Bench基准测试中优于现有最先进模型InfLLM，并在多项任务中超越RAG，同时在10M tokens的规模上成功实现检索，展示了其在处理长序列上下文中的优越性能。该架构为探索人类记忆机制提供了一个新的计算框架。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无限上下文长度的计算方式及其与RAG（检索增强生成）的对比

不同观点：
• MacsHeadroom认为无限上下文长度是通过使其计算受限（compute bound）而不是内存受限（memory bound）来实现的。这种方法可能会增加运行时间，因此他质疑在什么情况下选择这种方法比使用RAG更合适。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点之一是无限上下文长度的实现方式，即通过增加计算资源的使用来突破内存限制。
• 另一个值得注意的点是这种方法与RAG的对比，RAG是一种通过检索机制来增强生成模型效果的技术。MacsHeadroom对在什么情况下选择计算受限的无限上下文长度而不是RAG提出了疑问，表明在实际应用中可能需要权衡运行时间和资源消耗。
• 例子包括对计算受限和内存受限两种方式的比较，以及在不同应用场景下如何选择合适的技术方案。

EM-LLM: Human-inspired Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs
This repository contains a version of the code for EM-LLM, published in
ICLR 2025
:
[openreview link]
.
Quick Links
Overview
Usage
Citation
Overview
While typical LLMs struggle with processing extensive contexts, the human brain excels at organising and retrieving experiences spanning a lifetime. In this work, we introduce EM-LLM, an architecture that integrates key aspects of human episodic memory and event cognition into LLMs with
no fine-tuning
, enabling them to handle practically infinite context lengths while maintaining computational efficiency. EM-LLM organises sequences of tokens into coherent episodic events using a combination of Bayesian surprise and graph-theoretic boundary refinement in an online fashion. When needed, these events are retrieved through a two-stage memory process, combining similarity-based and temporally contiguous retrieval for efficient and human-like access to relevant information. Experiments on the LongBench and
$\infty$
-Bench benchmarks demonstrate EM-LLM's superior performance, consistently outperforming the SOTA retrieval model InfLLM across various baseline LLMs. In addition, EM-LLM
outperforms RAG
in a wide range of tasks, while requiring similar resources. Notably, EM-LLM's performance even
surpasses full-context models
in most tasks, while successfully performing retrieval across
10M tokens
- a scale computationally infeasible for such models. Our analysis reveals strong correlations between EM-LLM's event segmentation and human-perceived events, suggesting a bridge between this artificial system and its biological counterpart, thereby offering a novel computational framework for exploring human memory mechanisms.
Architecture
Figure 1:
Architecture of memory formation and retrieval in each LLM layer.
Formation:
Input sequence is initially segmented via surprise (purple dashed lines in ①), then segmentation is refined based on group theoretic metrics (green dashed lines in ②). Initial tokens and local context are preserved.
Retrieval:
via both k-NN search ③ and selecting contiguous events from episodic memory ④.

here

(Left)

(Right)

43943928.article_summary: EM-LLM是一种受人类情景记忆启发的大语言模型架构，能够在不微调的情况下处理几乎无限长度的上下文，同时保持计算效率。该模型通过结合贝叶斯 surprise 和图论边界优化将输入序列组织成连贯的情景事件，并在需要时通过基于相似性和时间连续性的两阶段记忆过程进行检索。实验表明，EM-LLM在LongBench和∞-Bench基准测试中优于现有最先进模型InfLLM，并在多项任务中超越RAG，同时在10M tokens的规模上成功实现检索，展示了其在处理长序列上下文中的优越性能。该架构为探索人类记忆机制提供了一个新的计算框架。
43943928.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无限上下文长度的计算方式及其与RAG（检索增强生成）的对比

不同观点：
• MacsHeadroom认为无限上下文长度是通过使其计算受限（compute bound）而不是内存受限（memory bound）来实现的。这种方法可能会增加运行时间，因此他质疑在什么情况下选择这种方法比使用RAG更合适。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点之一是无限上下文长度的实现方式，即通过增加计算资源的使用来突破内存限制。
• 另一个值得注意的点是这种方法与RAG的对比，RAG是一种通过检索机制来增强生成模型效果的技术。MacsHeadroom对在什么情况下选择计算受限的无限上下文长度而不是RAG提出了疑问，表明在实际应用中可能需要权衡运行时间和资源消耗。
• 例子包括对计算受限和内存受限两种方式的比较，以及在不同应用场景下如何选择合适的技术方案。

• [efilife] 和 [floundy] 都提到了“正常人”和“少数例外”的概念，这表明讨论中涉及对多数人意见和少数人感受之间平衡的考虑。

data.title: I Want to Love Linux. It Doesn't Love Me Back
data.author: MrVandemar
data.article_summary: 本文是一位长期使用Linux的盲人用户对该系统在无障碍使用方面存在问题的批评与反思。作者肯定了Linux的优点，如配置文件透明、系统可自由定制等，但也指出其在无障碍支持上的严重缺陷。文章详细描述了Linux在启动、登录、音频栈及控制台语音等方面的各种问题，如Orca屏幕阅读器无法持久运行、音频设置混乱、Speakup控制台语音支持不足等。作者强调，这些问题并非简单的bug，而是长期的忽视。尽管Linux提倡自由和定制，但对于盲人用户而言，使用Linux意味着需要手动配置、编写脚本和修复系统，增加了极大的负担。最终，作者对Linux无障碍支持的现状感到疲惫和失望。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux在视觉障碍用户中的可访问性问题及其整体用户体验

不同观点：
• **关于针对视觉障碍用户的Linux发行版**：
   - chmod775提到有一些专门为视觉障碍用户开发的Linux发行版，如基于Ubuntu MATE的Accessible Coconut、基于Fedora的Vojtux和基于Debian的Emmabuntus，这些发行版可能解决了可访问性问题。
   - 这些发行版的存在表明Linux社区确实在为特定用户群体做努力，但也有用户需要自行制作系统镜像，缺乏开箱即用的便利性。

• **关于Orca屏幕阅读器的语音合成质量**：
   - chmod775认为Orca的语音合成质量较差，声音失真且机械化，质疑是否默认设置有问题。
   - arp242补充自己曾尝试设置文本转语音工具，但遇到问题并最终放弃，认为Linux在该领域的开发不够完善。

• **Linux整体用户体验的讨论**：
   - chronid认为Linux的用户体验在变差，特别是在加密系统上的休眠问题和安全启动等安全措施带来的不便。
   - washadjeffmad通过引用Nelson Mandela对“Ubuntu”的解释，批评Canonical及其Ubuntu Desktop在服务和使命上的转变，认为其忽视了社区需求。
   - andrewmcwatters指出Linux从未被认为是“一用就灵”的系统，而是需要用户不断折腾和调试的。

• **关于命令行界面与桌面会话的适用性**：
   - prmoustache质疑盲人用户为何需要桌面会话，认为命令行界面可能更适合盲人用户，并指出终端复用器如tmux和screen的潜在不足。
   - 其他用户未直接回应此观点，但chmod775和arp242的评论表明Linux在某些情况下的命令行工具确实存在可访问性问题。

补充讨论：
• **关于Linux音频系统的争议**：
   - tomjuggler对Linux上的音频系统表示不满，认为Wayland多年来的发展仍然不尽如人意。
   - joemazerino则对作者的体验表示同情，并好奇视觉障碍用户在Windows或Mac上的体验如何。

争议焦点：
• Linux在视觉障碍用户群体中的可访问性问题及其背后的原因，特别是针对Orca语音合成质量、桌面会话与命令行界面的适用性等具体问题存在不同看法。

总结：评论中主要讨论了Linux在视觉障碍用户群体中的可访问性现状及问题，指出了特定发行版和工具的存在与不足，并探讨了Linux整体用户体验和音频系统的问题。争议点集中在Orca的语音质量、桌面会话的必要性以及Linux的可访问性开发是否足够完善。

I Want to Love Linux. It Doesn’t Love Me Back: Post 1 – Built for Control, But Not for People
Published on
May 10, 2025
Linux Is Already Broken Before You Even Start
I love Linux.
I use Linux.
It has its advantages.
It’s responsive—sometimes.
Some things just work plain better.
Settings being stored in actual config files instead of opaque registries? That’s an
accessibility win
.
When something breaks, you don’t have to reinstall the whole OS like you would on Windows.
Most importantly:
it’s mine.
To do with as I please. To fix, break, rebuild, and own.
And let me be clear:
This post is
not
an attack on the people who maintain Linux accessibility.
I have huge respect for every single person who’s ever written a patch to Orca, BRLTTY, speech-dispatcher, AT-SPI, or any of the dozens of tools that make it possible to use Linux without sight.
They are often doing it for free, in their spare time, while fighting upstream changes, toolkit breakage, and general apathy from distros and desktop makers.
They are heroes for making it work
despite
all that.
And before any neckbeards leap in with:
“Be the change you want to see.”
“Code it yourself.”
Yeah. I know.
I try. When I have the spoons. When I understand the stack well enough to do more than write a bug report titled “it no work.”
But I shouldn’t have to.
And if that’s all you have to say?
Stop reading. I don’t care.
Let me be blunt:
This isn’t a rant from someone who gave Linux a shot and bounced off.
This is from someone who’s used Linux full-time for years as a blind user—someone who knows the system inside out, who has made it work through manual configuration, scripting, rebuilding broken packages, and sheer force of will.
And still?
I’m exhausted.
Because Linux doesn’t fail at the margins.
It fails at the very first step.
Before you open a terminal.
Before you write a line of code.
Before you even get logged in—the basic, day-one functionality of accessibility is already broken, decaying, or actively getting worse.
“It Just Works” — The First Lie
Linux “just works”—if you can see.
If you’re blind?
You boot into a live image and get nothing.
No speech. No braille. No login prompt feedback. Maybe Orca starts, maybe not.
Maybe you know the shortcut (Alt+Super+S?) but does that even work in this session type?
Is it Wayland? Is it X11? Is the screen reader bound to a key combo that doesn’t exist on your keyboard?
You open the installer?
“Next. Button. Button. Button. Button.”
That’s all Orca says.
Ubuntu MATE 12.04 had a working, labeled, navigable installer.
Ubuntu MATE 24.04? It’s garbage.
No headings. No structure. No sense of where you are. Just unlabeled buttons and blank space.
This isn’t a bug.
This is neglect.
Logging In Is a Joke Now
Used to be, on Ubuntu MATE, you could hit Alt+Super+S at the login screen and get Orca.
Now?
You hear a drumbeat sound.
No speech.
No braille.
No way to start the screen reader.
No visual confirmation—unless you can see.
And if you do start Orca manually after boot?
It doesn’t persist.
It used to—years ago. Now? Every login you start from scratch.
You want persistence?
You download a random shell script from GitHub.
You patch your own session files.
You maintain the config yourself—because no distro ships it working.
The Audio Stack: Now With Extra Failure
Let’s say Orca does start.
Now the audio stack kicks in.
Is it PipeWire?
PulseAudio?
Is ALSA enabled? Is the correct fallback sink selected?
Is the audio device owned by root? Is the socket exposed to your session?
Who knows. Because:
Pulse loads the wrong output.
PipeWire can’t access your card.
Speech Dispatcher is stuck waiting for a disconnected device.
You log in and get nothing. No error. Just silence.
Want to debug it?
You can’t—because you can’t hear anything.
So you grab your phone, take a picture of the screen, feed it to an image captioning AI, and hope it tells you whether the error dialog says “Audio device unavailable” or “Session startup failed.”
This is normal now.
Console Speech Exists—But It’s Never Set Up
Technically, yes, you can get speech on the console.
Linux Speakup exists. It’s been in the kernel for decades. It supports software and hardware synths.
You can log into a tty and use your machine without graphics.
But no one enables it.
Your distro doesn’t load
speakup_soft
.
It doesn’t start
espeakup
.
It doesn’t ship the synth module in the initrd.
The audio system might not even initialize before
espeakup
starts, so it fails silently.
So even if you drop to single-user mode—say, because the GUI broke—you get nothing.
Not even an error.
You sit there with no speech, no fallback, hoping you can remember the exact keystrokes to get to a working shell blind.
You want it to work? You have to:
Install and enable Speakup.
Patch the initrd.
Rebuild your audio stack.
Debug the TTY config.
Pray you didn’t forget a kernel module.
Scripts for Everything. Everything.
You want:
Persistent Orca? Script.
Speakup at boot? Script.

data.title: AI-powered headphones offer group translation with voice cloning and 3D audio
data.author: daoboy
data.article_summary: 大学 of Washington的研究团队开发了一种名为Spatial Speech Translation的耳机系统，能够在公共空间中同时翻译多人的讲话，并保留每个人声音的方向和特质。该系统利用现成的降噪耳机和内置麦克风，通过算法分离不同说话者，实时追踪他们的移动，并在2-4秒的延迟后播放翻译内容。该系统在10个室内外场景中进行了测试，用户反馈优于不具备空间追踪功能的翻译模型。目前，该系统适用于常见语言，并计划扩展至约100种语言。此技术旨在消除文化间的语言障碍，未来还将进一步优化翻译速度和处理专业术语的能力。

AI-powered headphones offer group translation with voice cloning and 3D spatial audio
by Stefan Milne,
University of Washington
Credit: University of Washington
Tuochao Chen, a University of Washington doctoral student, recently toured a museum in Mexico. Chen doesn't speak Spanish, so he ran a translation app on his phone and pointed the microphone at the tour guide. But even in a museum's relative quiet, the surrounding noise was too much. The resulting text was useless.
Various technologies have emerged lately promising fluent translation, but none of these solved Chen's problem of
public spaces
. Meta's new glasses, for instance, function only with an isolated speaker; they
play an automated voice translation
after the speaker finishes.
Now, Chen and a team of UW researchers have designed
a headphone system that translates several speakers
at once, while preserving the direction and qualities of people's voices. The team built the system, called Spatial Speech Translation, with off-the-shelf noise-canceling headphones fitted with microphones. The team's algorithms separate out the different speakers in a space and follow them as they move, translate their speech and play it back with a 2-4 second delay.
University of Washington researchers designed a headphone system that translates several people speaking at once, following them as they move and preserving the direction and qualities of their voices. The team built the system, called Spatial Speech Translation, with off-the-shelf noise-cancelling headphones fitted with microphones. Credit: Chen et al./CHI '25
The
team presented its research
Apr. 30 at the ACM CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems in Yokohama, Japan. The code for the proof-of-concept device is available for others to build on. "Other translation tech is built on the assumption that only one person is speaking," said senior author Shyam Gollakota, a UW professor in the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering. "But in the real world, you can't have just one robotic voice talking for multiple people in a room. For the first time, we've preserved the sound of each person's voice and the direction it's coming from."
The system makes three innovations. First, when turned on, it immediately detects how many speakers are in an indoor or outdoor space.
"Our algorithms work a little like radar," said lead author Chen, a UW doctoral student in the Allen School. "So they're scanning the space in 360 degrees and constantly determining and updating whether there's one person or six or seven."
The system then translates the speech and maintains the expressive qualities and volume of each
speaker
's voice while running on a device, such mobile devices with an Apple M2 chip like laptops and Apple Vision Pro. (The team avoided using cloud computing because of the privacy concerns with
voice
cloning.) Finally, when speakers move their heads, the system continues to track the direction and qualities of their voices as they change.
The system functioned when tested in 10 indoor and outdoor settings. And in a 29-participant test, the users preferred the system over models that didn't track speakers through space.
In a separate user test, most participants preferred a delay of 3-4 seconds, since the system made more errors when translating with a delay of 1-2 seconds. The team is working to reduce the speed of translation in future iterations. The system currently only works on commonplace speech, not specialized language such as technical jargon. For this paper, the team worked with Spanish, German and French—but previous work on
translation
models has shown they can be trained to translate around 100 languages.
"This is a step toward breaking down the
language barriers
between cultures," Chen said. "So if I'm walking down the street in Mexico, even though I don't speak Spanish, I can translate all the people's voices and know who said what."
Qirui Wang, a research intern at HydroX AI and a UW undergraduate in the Allen School while completing this research, and Runlin He, a UW doctoral student in the Allen School, are also co-authors on this paper.

Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
(2025).

43944743.article_summary: 大学 of Washington的研究团队开发了一种名为Spatial Speech Translation的耳机系统，能够在公共空间中同时翻译多人的讲话，并保留每个人声音的方向和特质。该系统利用现成的降噪耳机和内置麦克风，通过算法分离不同说话者，实时追踪他们的移动，并在2-4秒的延迟后播放翻译内容。该系统在10个室内外场景中进行了测试，用户反馈优于不具备空间追踪功能的翻译模型。目前，该系统适用于常见语言，并计划扩展至约100种语言。此技术旨在消除文化间的语言障碍，未来还将进一步优化翻译速度和处理专业术语的能力。

主要讨论点：对核聚变研究进展的评价及相关技术问题的讨论

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
  - edran认为此次更新很有价值，并期待后续版本，同时推荐了Pacific Fusion的相关白皮书。
  - jamiek88对Max Planck研究所的新Squids设计感到兴奋，认为其借鉴了现有仿星器的经验。
  - wonderwonder表示对能源领域的快速发展感到兴奋，后悔没有专注于这个行业。

• 技术质疑与现实考量：
  - CGMthrowaway指出NIF主要是一个核武器研究项目，而非发电厂原型，并列举了实现聚变发电所需的多项技术改进。
  - dale_glass提醒注意“收支平衡”的不同定义，强调反应堆系统整体的能源收支平衡更为重要。
  - 0xbadcafebee对“商业聚变能源还有30年”的说法表示怀疑，指出这一预测已存在多年。
  - damnitbuilds质疑当前进展是否真的能带来实际可用的聚变电力。

• 具体实验与技术细节：
  - actinium226对NIF在2000-2020年间的实验空白表示疑问，询问是否有其他托卡马克实验。
  - mapt询问First Light Fusion的第三台机器如何融入当前进展，并对其使用“枪”发射项目ile的设计表示好奇。

• 其他相关讨论：
  - gene-h提到有关NIF最近实现增益约4.4和燃料燃烧约10%的传闻，认为这值得关注。
  - londons_explore开玩笑询问是否有关于“到2100年地球上聚变能源占全球能源供应1%以上”的投注赔率。
  - UltraSane认为应将用于聚变研究的资金转投于下一代裂变电站和液态盐反应堆。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了多个具体技术概念，如激光效率、增益、燃料燃烧比例、q-plasma和q-total等，显示出对聚变技术细节的不同关注点。
- 争议焦点在于当前聚变研究的实际应用价值以及其与核武器研究的关系。
- 不同设计和实验（如NIF、托卡马克、Squids、First Light Fusion）之间的比较也是讨论的重要部分。

data.title: Reverse engineering the 386 processor's prefetch queue circuitry
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文详细介绍了1985年英特尔推出的386处理器的预取队列电路。386处理器是x86架构中的首款32位处理器，通过一个16字节的指令预取队列来提高性能。预取队列在指令执行前从内存中获取指令，避免处理器等待内存响应。队列中的增量器电路负责递增内存指针，具有复杂的高性能设计。预取队列还包括一个用于数据对齐的大型网络和用于符号扩展的紧凑电路。芯片的左侧主要是预取单元，其中的电路重复32次以处理每个位，垂直数据线连接各功能块。预取队列的核心是16字节的存储区，数据对齐网络占用了较大空间，而符号扩展电路则较为不规则。

43946824.article_content:
In 1985, Intel introduced the groundbreaking 386 processor, the first 32-bit processor in the x86 architecture.
To improve performance, the 386 has a 16-byte instruction prefetch queue.
The purpose of the prefetch queue is to fetch instructions from memory before they are needed,
so the processor usually doesn't need to wait on memory while executing instructions.
Instruction prefetching takes advantage of times when the processor is "thinking" and the memory bus would otherwise be unused.
In this article, I look at the 386's prefetch queue circuitry in detail.
One interesting circuit is the incrementer, which adds 1 to a pointer to step through memory.
This sounds easy enough, but the incrementer uses complicated circuitry for high performance.
The prefetch queue uses a large network
to shift bytes around so they are properly aligned.
It also has a compact circuit to extend signed 8-bit and 16-bit
numbers to 32 bits.
There aren't any major discoveries in this post, but if you're interested in low-level circuits and dynamic logic, keep reading.
The photo below shows the 386's shiny fingernail-sized silicon die under a microscope.
Although it may look like an aerial view of a strangely-zoned city, the die photo reveals the functional blocks
of the chip.
The Prefetch Unit in the upper left is the relevant block.
In this post, I'll discuss the
prefetch queue circuitry (highlighted in red), skipping over the prefetch control circuitry to the right.
The Prefetch Unit receives data from the Bus Interface Unit (upper right) that communicates with memory.
The Instruction Decode Unit receives prefetched instructions from the Prefetch Unit, byte by byte, and decodes the
opcodes for execution.
This die photo of the 386 shows the location of the registers. Click this image (or any other) for a larger version.
The left quarter of the chip consists of stripes of circuitry that appears much more orderly than the rest of the chip.
This grid-like appearance arises because
each functional block is constructed (for the most part) by repeating the same circuit 32 times, once for each bit, side by side.
Vertical data lines run up and down, in groups of 32 bits, connecting the functional blocks.
To make this work, each circuit must fit into the same width on the die; this layout constraint forces the circuit
designers to develop a circuit that uses this width efficiently without exceeding the allowed width.
The circuitry for the prefetch queue uses the same approach: each circuit is 66 µm wide
1
and repeated 32 times.
As will be seen, fitting the prefetch circuitry into this fixed width requires some layout tricks.
What the prefetcher does
The purpose of the prefetch unit is to speed up performance by reading instructions from memory before they are needed,
so the processor won't need to wait to get instructions from memory.
Prefetching takes advantage of times when the memory bus is otherwise idle, minimizing conflict with other instructions
that are reading or writing data.
In the 386, prefetched instructions are stored in a 16-byte queue, consisting of four 32-bit blocks.
2
The diagram below zooms in on the prefetcher and shows its main components.
You can see how the same circuit (in most cases) is repeated 32 times, forming vertical bands.
At the top are 32 bus lines from the Bus Interface Unit. These lines provide the connection between the datapath and
external memory, via the Bus Interface Unit.
These lines form a triangular pattern as the 32 horizontal lines on the right branch off and form 32 vertical lines, one for each bit.
Next are the fetch pointer and the limit register, with a circuit to check if the fetch pointer has
reached the limit.
Note that the two low-order bits (on the right) of the incrementer and limit check circuit are
missing.
At the bottom of the incrementer, you can see that some bit positions have a blob of circuitry missing from others,
breaking the pattern of repeated blocks.
The 16-byte prefetch queue is below the incrementer. Although this memory is the heart of the prefetcher, its
circuitry takes up a relatively small area.
A close-up of the prefetcher with the main blocks labeled. At the right, the prefetcher receives control signals.
The bottom part of the prefetcher shifts data to align it as needed.
A 32-bit value can be split across two 32-bit
rows of the prefetch buffer.
To handle this, the prefetcher includes a data shift network to shift and align its data.
This network occupies a lot of space, but there is no active circuitry here: just a grid of horizontal and vertical wires.
Finally, the sign extend circuitry converts a signed 8-bit or 16-bit value into a signed 16-bit or 32-bit value
as needed.
You can see that the sign extend circuitry is highly irregular, especially in the middle.
A latch stores the output of the prefetch queue for use by the rest of the datapath.

data.title: Show HN: Code Claude Code
data.author: sean_
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为`codesys`的Python SDK，用于与Claude CLI工具交互。该SDK提供了简单接口来运行Claude，支持所有Claude CLI选项，并允许自动或手动处理输出流。主要功能包括通过Agent类执行提示，支持指定工作目录和允许的工具列表。使用示例展示了如何生成任务计划并执行，包括自动流式输出。安装需通过`pip install codesys`，并要求Python 3.8+和配置好的Claude CLI工具。SDK还提供了多种运行Claude的方法，如`run`和`run_with_tools`，可根据需要自定义参数和输出格式。

不同观点：
• anotherpaulg 认为该项目有一个不错的紧凑代码库，并且支持通过Python或命令行进行脚本编写，非常强大。他提供了相关文档和演示视频，展示该项目在支持新编程语言方面的强大功能。
• justanotheratom 提出了项目名称是否源自"Bob Loblaw"的文字游戏，带有调侃性质，可能与流行文化有关。
• edmundsauto 回应了其他用户对项目源代码查找困难的问题，提供了源代码的链接。

• divan 将该项目与其他类似项目（RooCode任务编排器和claude-task-master）进行比较，认为任务编排是每个代理AI解决方案的必备功能，并提供了相关链接以供比较。
• rvz 对项目的实用性提出了质疑，认为缺乏测试使得项目不可靠，存在数百个bug，并且不符合“清洁代码”和测试驱动开发的原则。他强调，AI时代的软件更需要严格的测试，以降低风险。

data.title: Prolog's Eternal September (2017)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 作者最近意识到，他在Stack Overflow上回答Prolog问题的方式违反了平台规则，且这种做法实际上适得其反。许多初学者在Stack Overflow上提问Prolog作业问题，但他们并不查看已有解决方案，只是希望有人替他们完成作业。作者认为，这反映了一个更深层次的问题：Prolog是必修课，但教授本身也不理解它，因此无法有效教学。作者希望创造一个更建设性的学习环境，提出两个建议：建立一个小型的解决方案数据库，每个解决方案都有详细注解，帮助理解基础和高级概念；为教授设计一系列教学幻灯片，即使他们不太懂Prolog也能使用。作者希望通过这种方式改善Prolog的教学和学习体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Prolog的教育与应用，以及在编程教育中的挑战

不同观点：
• **Neilv**：认为初学者在Stack Overflow上只想找人代做作业，而非寻找现有解决方案。AI正在替代懒惰的学生完成作业，形成一种循环，最终损害了认真学习者的利益。
• **Disambiguation**：建议将LLMs（大型语言模型）与Prolog结合，利用LLMs生成Prolog代码来解决推理问题，尽管自己尚未实现这一想法。
• **Melenaboija**：分享了自己20年前的逻辑课程经验，强调从基础开始逐步构建对Prolog的理解，并认为这种方法非常有效。
• **Chuckadams**：主张在现代类型系统的背景下教授Prolog，并指出由于学校不重视，很难找到真正理解Prolog的教师。
• **Crustycoder**：认为Prolog长期以来被视为学术工具，难以推广。建议直接向实际编写代码的开发者推广Prolog，并通过实际例子和与已知概念（如SQL或函数式编程）的关联来教学。
• **Cbarrick**：提出需要对Prolog的模块系统进行创新，类似于Clojure对Lisp的创新。
• **Arch-TK**：指出不仅Prolog，C语言也存在教师不理解教学内容的问题，尤其是那些没有兴趣深入学习但自认为精通的人。
• **Subjectsigma**：推荐了YouTube频道，认为其内容从初学者到专家级都有覆盖，能够帮助解决Prolog教学问题。
• **Oh_my_goodness**：认为Q&A网站如果对提问者持敌对态度，会变得有毒和难以忍受，并通过自身经历指出新用户涌入和部分老用户自大是问题所在。
• **JadeNB**：认为不应该为了迎合不理解Prolog的教师而降低教学标准，建议通过说服教师Prolog的有趣性和重要性来提高教学质量。
• **CyberDildonics**：质疑Prolog本身的价值，认为如果学生学完后不再使用，可能说明Prolog并不实用，编程应更注重实际软件构建而非语言的巧妙性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了Prolog在教育中的困境，包括教师不理解、学生学后不用等问题。
• 提出了多种改进Prolog教学的方法，如结合现代类型系统、利用AI生成代码、通过实际例子和与其他已知概念的关联来教学。
• 还讨论了Q&A网站的社区氛围问题，指出对新手友好和避免敌对态度的重要性。

Daniel's Blog
Home
Archives
Search
Feed
About
I realized recently that the way I have been handling answers to Prolog questions on Stack Overflow contravenes the rules. I don’t mind ignoring rules if it serves a higher purpose, but I have also come to realize that it actually is counterproductive.
There is a constant flow of pre-beginner questions about Prolog on Stack Overflow. The questions I’m referring to typically sound like this:
“
my professor said a few incoherent things about Prolog and here’s my assignment and I don’t know where to start.” The pre-beginners are not at Stack Overflow to look at existing solutions (which is what Stack Overflow wants you to do). They just want someone to do their homework for them.. They don’t come back later or develop a deeper appreciation for Prolog. Some of this is unavoidable, but the flow is very high.
As much as I would like to (and have tried to) take the opportunity to foster an interest in Prolog, their questions are actually a symptom of a totally different problem that simply cannot be addressed within
SO
. I think the underlying problem is that Prolog is part of a mandatory curriculum, but the professor doesn’t understand it.
How do you teach something you don’t understand?
I would like to live in a world where professors consider Prolog worth knowing and put in the effort. That probably isn’t realistic. If I can’t have that, I would at least like to live in a world where students’ first or only exposure to Prolog is something more constructive than
“
Look how weird and confusing this thing is!”
I’m not in higher education, so I don’t know how to approach these problems. I would love to hear some ideas. But my first thought is a two-pronged approach:
A smallish (less than 10) solution database, where each solution is somehow annotated so that you can figure out both really low-level things (variables are uppercase) and really high-level things (why an accumulator is used). The idea is that it should be possible to answer any question, no matter how obvious, by mousing over things in the solution database.
A set of slides for use by professors to teach Prolog without really knowing it. There would be a few different versions (one class session, three class sessions) and a moratorium on providing solutions on Stack Overflow, instead pointing people who ask to the solution database.
Have other ideas? Please send me an email, let’s talk.

data.title: Comparison of C/POSIX standard library implementations for Linux
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 这篇文章对比了Linux上几种C/POSIX标准库实现，包括musl、uClibc、dietlibc和glibc，重点比较了它们的功能丰富度与代码膨胀问题。对比涵盖了静态和动态程序大小、性能基准、可配置功能集、线程行为、ABI兼容性、算法实现、特性支持、目标架构、构建环境以及安全性等方面。总体来看，musl在代码大小和性能上表现较好，glibc功能最全但较臃肿，uClibc和dietlibc则在轻量级应用中有优势。文章还提到未来将进行更详细的性能测试并纳入其他库如Bionic。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发者对各类libc库性能、许可证和维护状态的看法

不同观点：
• pizlonator认为，从系统自带的glibc切换到自行构建的musl libc后，出现了1-2%的性能下降。他推测可能是由于glibc的memcpy/memmove/memset函数优化得更好，但不确定。他还指出Fil-C运行时使用了自己的分配器，因此性能问题不应归因于分配器。

• ObscureScience指出，相关的libc对比表已经过时，信息可能不再具有参考价值，因此对其实际相关性表示怀疑。

• thrtythreeforty强调，对比表应该首先列出各个libc库的许可证。他提到dietlibc因为采用GPLv2许可证而成为"非 starter"（不考虑使用），因为即使是GPL支持者也理解这在实际应用中的限制，相比之下GNU的libc采用的是更宽松的LGPL协议。

• moomin简单表达了对Cosmopolitan libc未被提及的遗憾。

• jay-barronville同意ObscureScience的观点，指出libc对比表已经长期未维护，并提供了musl libc官网的链接以支持这一说法。

• edam讽刺地指出，该对比表很显然是musl的作者制作的，暗示可能存在偏见。

• snickerer总结认为glibc虽然"臃肿"但速度快，这是一种"出乎意料的组合"，并向其他开发者求证这一看法是否正确。

补充讨论：
• 对libc库性能的比较，尤其是glibc和musl之间的性能差异，是讨论的核心。
• 许可证问题也是一些开发者关心的重要因素，特别是对于GPL和LGPL的偏好或限制。
• 对比表的时效性和潜在的作者偏见也是讨论中提到的值得注意的问题。

43946149.article_content:
Comparison of C/POSIX standard library implementations for Linux
A project of
Eta Labs
.
The table below and notes which follow are a comparison of some of
the different standard library implementations available for Linux,
with a particular focus on the balance between feature-richness and
bloat. I have tried to be fair and objective, but as I am the author
of
musl
, that may have
influenced my choice of which aspects to compare.
Future directions for this comparison include detailed performance

43946149.article_summary: 这篇文章对比了Linux上几种C/POSIX标准库实现，包括musl、uClibc、dietlibc和glibc，重点比较了它们的功能丰富度与代码膨胀问题。对比涵盖了静态和动态程序大小、性能基准、可配置功能集、线程行为、ABI兼容性、算法实现、特性支持、目标架构、构建环境以及安全性等方面。总体来看，musl在代码大小和性能上表现较好，glibc功能最全但较臃肿，uClibc和dietlibc则在轻量级应用中有优势。文章还提到未来将进行更详细的性能测试并纳入其他库如Bionic。
43946149.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发者对各类libc库性能、许可证和维护状态的看法

不同观点：
• pizlonator认为，从系统自带的glibc切换到自行构建的musl libc后，出现了1-2%的性能下降。他推测可能是由于glibc的memcpy/memmove/memset函数优化得更好，但不确定。他还指出Fil-C运行时使用了自己的分配器，因此性能问题不应归因于分配器。

• ObscureScience指出，相关的libc对比表已经过时，信息可能不再具有参考价值，因此对其实际相关性表示怀疑。

• thrtythreeforty强调，对比表应该首先列出各个libc库的许可证。他提到dietlibc因为采用GPLv2许可证而成为"非 starter"（不考虑使用），因为即使是GPL支持者也理解这在实际应用中的限制，相比之下GNU的libc采用的是更宽松的LGPL协议。

• moomin简单表达了对Cosmopolitan libc未被提及的遗憾。

• jay-barronville同意ObscureScience的观点，指出libc对比表已经长期未维护，并提供了musl libc官网的链接以支持这一说法。

• edam讽刺地指出，该对比表很显然是musl的作者制作的，暗示可能存在偏见。

• snickerer总结认为glibc虽然"臃肿"但速度快，这是一种"出乎意料的组合"，并向其他开发者求证这一看法是否正确。

补充讨论：
• 对libc库性能的比较，尤其是glibc和musl之间的性能差异，是讨论的核心。
• 许可证问题也是一些开发者关心的重要因素，特别是对于GPL和LGPL的偏好或限制。
• 对比表的时效性和潜在的作者偏见也是讨论中提到的值得注意的问题。

data.author: kobieps
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flutter开发中的技术选择与偏好

不同观点：
• doawoo认为Riverpod相较于无状态组件加Hooks过于复杂，增加了心智负担，并询问其他人偏好Riverpod的原因。
• 针对doawoo的观点，可能存在隐含的反对方见，认为Riverpod提供了更强大的状态管理能力，尽管复杂但适合大规模应用开发。

补充讨论：
• zerr提出了Flutter在美国不如在其他国家流行的问题，并将此现象与美国的JavaScript中心化开发文化联系起来，暗示技术选择的区域性偏好可能影响Flutter的普及。
• sgt关心Riverpod或其他状态管理方案是否能在Flutter Web中使用，表明对跨平台一致性的关注。
• account-5对数据库选择提出疑问，建议使用SQLite而非Drift，关注点在于具体技术实现的简便性与适用性。

争议焦点：
• Riverpod的使用必要性与复杂性之间的平衡是争议的焦点，部分开发者认为其提供了更好的状态管理，而其他开发者则觉得增加了不必要的复杂度。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 不同地区（如美国与发展中国家）对Flutter的接受程度差异，可能受到技术生态和开发文化的影响。
• 数据库选择（SQLite vs Drift）反映了开发者在选择工具时对简单性和功能性的权衡。

data.title: A Critical Look at MCP
data.author: ablekh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了对MCP（Model Context Protocol）的批评和实施中的问题。MCP旨在标准化LLM（大语言模型）与外界交互的方式，类似于USB-C为设备提供的标准化连接。尽管MCP及类似协议（如IBM的ACP和Google的A2A）快速发展，但作者指出其文档和SDK质量低下，设计决策和协议规范不成熟。作者特别批评了MCP的HTTP传输方案（SSE+HTTP和所谓的"Streamable HTTP"），认为应使用WebSockets来替代。作者尝试用Golang实现MCP服务器，但因协议不完善而遇到困难，认为MCP的实施过程存在严重问题，呼吁改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Model Context Protocol）的现状、成熟度、及其与现有技术标准（如REST、JSON-RPC等）的比较

不同观点：
• hirsin认为，LLM（大型语言模型）领域的开发者正在快速推进新软件范式，但忽视了已有的技术标准（如DLLs, gRPC, SOAP等），并预计该技术会在几个月后逐渐成熟。
• mattw1810指出，MCP本应一开始就采用无状态的HTTP，大多数服务器不需要在请求/会话级别保持状态。
• aristofun认为，AI开发主要由非专业软件工程师的人员推动，导致许多AI项目看似是短期内的个人项目，缺乏软件工程标准。
• _QrE赞同上述观点，并对MCP网站上缺乏实质内容感到困惑，认为RFCs虽然难读，但比简单的“使用我们的SDK库”要好。
• keithwhor认为，MCP作为连接LLM和工具的通用方式具有潜力，但在实践中遇到许多问题（如认证、流式响应、工具验证等）。他质疑MCP相对于REST API的优势，并担心用户安装不可信的第三方集成。
• dend澄清，MCP的授权部分已经过时，他们已经与Anthropic和安全社区合作更新了相关规范。
• practal认为，MCP的schema非常有用，但很快会遇到不支持的功能，并希望通过MCP实现无前端的Practal。
• fendy3002认为，MCP可以简单解释为JSON-RPC协议，并质疑为何没人这样解释或推广。
• justanotheratom质疑MCP相对于OpenAPI规范的优势。
• punkpeye作为MCP注册表的创始人，承认MCP在早期阶段存在很多问题，但指出其快速发展并提供了相关资源。
• shivawu认为，技术初期往往是平庸且充满问题的，需要大量努力和时间来改进，如同JavaScript早期版本一样。
• traviscline正在开发Go程序/工具，以描述现有服务器的语言中立方式，并希望借此引入一些规范。
• hrpnk关注MCP服务器的实际实现，认为许多供应商只是为了LLM兼容性而包装REST API，缺乏工程实践。
• Scotrix对MCP的实现和错误提示不满，认为没有清晰的规范，需要通过试验和错误来解决问题。

补充讨论：
• MCP的成熟度和实际应用中的问题是被广泛讨论的焦点，尤其是在认证、工具验证和服务器实现方面。
• 不同开发者对MCP相对于现有技术（如REST、JSON-RPC）的优势和不足存在争议。
• MCP的快速普及与其不成熟的状态之间的矛盾是讨论的另一个重要方面。
• 社区对MCP规范的更新和改进抱有期待，同时也提供了资源和工具来帮助其发展。

43945993.article_content:
Raz Blog
A Critical Look at MCP
"MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI
applications. Just as USB-C provides a standardized way to connect your devices to various peripherals and accessories, MCP
provides a standardized way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools."
― Anthropic
TL;DR
I would like for this to turn out to be a skill issue on my part, and hope that I'm missing something.
During the past month,
MCP (Model Context Protocol)
, which would enable
LLMs to become agents and interact with the world, has really been blowing up. The idea is straightforward: let's standardize an
API for LLM/Agents to interact with the world and how to inform the LLM/Agent about it.
Things are moving really fast, and IBM recently released their own "orthogonal standard" to MCP
called
Agent Communication Protocol (ACP)
, followed closely by Google
announcing
Agent2Agent (A2A)
.
MCP Servers and Clients are being built and published daily, and can be found at sites like
mcp.so
and
pulsemcp.com
.
However, I'm astonished by the apparent lack of mature engineering practices. All the major players spend billions of dollars on
training and tuning their models, only to turn around and, from what I can tell, have an interns write the documentation,
providing subpar SDKs and very little in terms of implementation guidance.
This trend seems to have continued with MCP, resulting in some very strange design decisions, poor documentation, and an even
worse specification of the actual protocols.
My conclusion is that the whole suggested setup for HTTP transport (SSE+HTTP and Streamable HTTP) should be thrown out and
replaced
with something that mimics stdio... Websockets.
Background
About three weeks ago, I decided to jump on the MCP bandwagon to give it a try and see how it could be used in our own
environment. I'm very much a person who wants to understand how things actually work under the hood before I start using
abstractions. Here we have a new protocol that works over different transports — how exciting!
Anthropic is the company behind the MCP standardization effort, and MCP seems to be one of the major reasons Anthropic's CEO is
thinking that most code will be written by LLMs within a year or so. The bet on coding tooling in particular seems to have been
the guiding principle of the standardization effort based on how it feels to work with it.
Protocol
Simply put, it is a JSON-RPC protocol with predefined methods/endpoints designed to be used in conjunction with an LLM. This is
not really the focus of this post, but there are things to be criticized about the protocol itself.
Transport
As with many applications post-2005, they're supposedly "local first" (
ironically
), and this seems to be very much the case with
MCP. Looking at the transport protocol, you get a sense of where
they're coming from—if their intention is to build LLM tools for coding on your laptop. They're probably looking at local IDEs (or
more realistically, Cursor or Windsurf) and how to have the LLM interact with the local file system, databases, editors, language
servers, and so on.
There are essentially two main transport protocols (or three):
stdio
"Something over HTTP, the web seems to be a thing we probably should support."
Stdio
Using stdio essentially means starting a local MCP Server, hooking up
stdout
and
stdin
pipes from the server to the client,
and starting to send JSON and using
stderr
for logging. It kind of breaks the Unix/Linux piping paradigm using these streams for
bidirectional communication. When bidirectional communication is needed, we usually reach for a socket, unix socket or even a net
socket.
However, it is straightforward and easy to reason about, works out of the box in all OSes, no need to deal with sockets, and so
on. So even if there is a critique to be made, I get it.
HTTP+SSE / Streamable HTTP
The HTTP transport is another story. There are two versions of the same mistake: HTTP+SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport, which is
being replaced by "Streamable HTTP" (a made-up term) that uses REST semantics with SSE. But with a whole lot of extra confusion
and corner cases on top.
It can be summarized as: "Since we like SSE for LLM streaming, we're not using WebSockets. Instead, we're effectively implementing
WebSockets on top of SSE and calling it 'Streamable HTTP' to make people think it's an accepted/known way of doing things."
They discuss the problems with WebSockets (and the reason for Streamable HTTP) in this
PR:
modelcontextprotocol/pull/206
, making some very
strange contortions and straw-man arguments to
not
use WebSockets. At least one other person in the thread seems to agree with
me:
modelcontextprotocol/pull/206#issuecomment-2766559523
.
A Descent into Madness
I set out to implement an MCP server in Golang. There isn't an official Go SDK, and I wanted to understand the protocol. This
turned out to be a mistake for mental hea

• justanotheratom质疑MCP相对于OpenAPI规范的优势。
• punkpeye作为MCP注册表的创始人，承认MCP在早期阶段存在很多问题，但指出其快速发展并提供了相关资源。
• shivawu认为，技术初期往往是平庸且充满问题的，需要大量努力和时间来改进，如同JavaScript早期版本一样。
• traviscline正在开发Go程序/工具，以描述现有服务器的语言中立方式，并希望借此引入一些规范。
• hrpnk关注MCP服务器的实际实现，认为许多供应商只是为了LLM兼容性而包装REST API，缺乏工程实践。
• Scotrix对MCP的实现和错误提示不满，认为没有清晰的规范，需要通过试验和错误来解决问题。

补充讨论：
• MCP的成熟度和实际应用中的问题是被广泛讨论的焦点，尤其是在认证、工具验证和服务器实现方面。
• 不同开发者对MCP相对于现有技术（如REST、JSON-RPC）的优势和不足存在争议。
• MCP的快速普及与其不成熟的状态之间的矛盾是讨论的另一个重要方面。
• 社区对MCP规范的更新和改进抱有期待，同时也提供了资源和工具来帮助其发展。

data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 本文报道了美国多个港口因特朗普关税政策导致进口大幅下降的情况。西雅图港专员Ryan Calkins表示，当前港口船只稀少，反映出关税对经济的实际影响，可能导致长滩港和洛杉矶港等主要港口货运量下降约35%。这种情况不仅威胁到与货运相关的工作岗位，还可能导致消费者面临价格上涨和产品短缺。专家警告，关税引发的航运放缓将像疫情初期一样影响美国各地区，首先冲击西海岸港口，随后蔓延至墨西哥湾和东海岸港口。尽管美国正与中方商讨可能降低关税的协议，但中方态度不明朗。
